expected: First feasible run: accuracy 0.750-0.765, time 8-13 s, complete=True. If accuracy falls below 0.753, raise to 10 epochs before testing anything else (see the H4.2.1 idea).
description: Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style port. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv, with whitening computed in prepare from training patches; Dirac init; 3 residual groups of 3 convs at widths 128/384/576; BatchNorm-GELU. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD, lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, batch size 1024, triangular LR schedule, 9 epochs, label smoothing 0.3. Data: the dataset stays on the GPU in fp16/channels_last; random crop (pad 2) runs on the GPU; derandomized alternating flip. No TTA and no torch.compile yet. Eval is a plain forward pass with no state changes. Build warms up eager kernels and cuDNN on synthetic tensors for train batch 1024 and eval B in {1, 1024}. This is the base recipe every other idea builds on.

expected: 8.5 epochs: accuracy drops 0.2-0.5 pp and time drops 4-8%. 10 epochs: accuracy rises about 0.5-0.8 pp and time rises about 11%.
description: On the E-port recipe, change only the epoch count: 9 → 8.5 if the port clears 0.753 with at least 0.3 pp margin, otherwise 9 → 10. Everything else stays identical, so this measures the local accuracy-vs-time slope that sets how far epochs can be cut.

expected: Time drops 10-25% (for example 10 s → 8 s). Accuracy stays within ±0.2 pp. Eval stays under 5 s for every B.
description: On the port, compile the model's forward+backward with torch.compile (mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs') in build. Compile and warm up on synthetic inputs for the train batch shape and the ragged last-batch shape, and in eval mode for B in {1, 7, 512, 1024} (mark the batch dimension dynamic for eval, or fall back to the eager model for eval). Also replace the per-param SGD loop with a foreach/fused SGD. Math stays unchanged.

expected: Accuracy +0.2-0.5 pp at under 2% extra time. That margin would later allow cutting about 0.5 epoch.
description: On the port at 9 epochs, add Lookahead/EMA of weights in the airbench96_faster style: update every 5 steps, alpha ramping as in the reference, final weights set to the EMA copy. All EMA state is created and reset in prepare. The forward pass is unchanged.

expected: Mean times within 2% of each other. Per-seed std 0.15-0.4 pp. Mean accuracy differs by under 0.15 pp because the seeds are identical; any difference reflects nondeterminism only.
description: Re-run the port recipe (or the current best feasible recipe) byte-identically, as a noise calibration. Record the per-seed accuracies from both runs to estimate per-seed std and run-to-run time drift. This sets the margin needed above 0.753 for the 40-seed judgment.
note: Settled by E003/E004: compiled training is bit-deterministic per seed (identical per-seed accuracies), so a byte-identical re-run measures zero noise; time drift E003 steady vs E004 <0.3%.

expected: Time drops by 0.2-0.5 s (about 3-5%) if recompiles were leaking into the timed region; otherwise no change. Accuracy unchanged within 0.1 pp, since only about 0.03 epoch of data is dropped.
description: On the compiled port, drop the ragged last batch, so every training step has the same shape, and verify via warm-up logging that no recompile or autotune happens inside prepare/train. Compare against the compiled port that warmed up only the main shape.
note: Settled by E004: ragged batch is already dropped (n//bs steps) and with channels_last warmup trials 0-2 train in 8.94/8.92/8.94 s; TORCH_LOGS=recompiles shows no recompiles in prepare/train.

expected: If H1.2 holds, accuracy rises 0.3-1 pp at about equal time, which buys roughly 1 epoch. Risk: worse accuracy at bs 2000 on CIFAR-100, or Newton-Schulz overhead adding over 5% time.
description: Explore. On the port backbone, switch the conv filters to Muon: Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum, lr about 0.24, momentum 0.6. Keep SGD for BatchNorm params, whitening bias and the head. Batch size 2000 with the same epoch count. Newton-Schulz runs in bf16 with a foreach-style batched implementation.

expected: Time drops 5-15%. Accuracy changes between -0.5 and +0.1 pp; a loss above 0.2 pp would refute H2.3.1.
description: Explore. On the port, apply progressive resizing: the first about 40% of epochs at 24 px, the next 30% at 28 px, the rest at 32 px (random-resized-crop on the GPU via F.interpolate). Warm up every resolution in build on synthetic data. Epoch count unchanged.

expected: Time falls about 4-6%, from 7.33 to about 6.9-7.0 s. Accuracy falls 0.15-0.4 pp to about 0.755-0.757, so the run stays feasible. A drop above 0.5 pp means the EMA+Muon recipe is steeper than H4.2.2 says, and epochs should not be cut further.
description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe (Muon + Lookahead/EMA + progressive resizing 24→28→32 px, 9 epochs), change only the epoch count from 9 to 8.5. Keep the resolution split as fractions of total steps (about 40/30/30%) and stretch the LR and EMA schedules to the new step count. Warm up every resolution in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path. Set torch._dynamo.config.error_on_recompile=True after build so a leak fails loudly. This spends part of E007's 0.60 pp margin and measures the slope with EMA and Muon on.

expected: Accuracy rises 0.1-0.4 pp (to about 0.760-0.763) with no change in time (±1%). A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.3.4 and buys about 0.5 epoch for the next trim. A gain under 0.1 pp means EMA already captures the low-LR benefit.
description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, change only the end of the LR schedule: decay linearly to exactly 0 instead of 0.07 of peak, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head). The warm-up, peak and Lookahead/EMA schedule stay unchanged. This tests whether EMA and a lower final LR are only partly redundant, which the E005 post-mortem predicts.

expected: Time falls 6-10% (to about 6.6-6.9 s). Accuracy falls 0.2-0.5 pp (to about 0.754-0.757). The idea succeeds if the time saved per pp lost is better than the epoch trim's, about 5% per 0.3 pp. A loss above 0.6 pp means 20 px is too coarse for 100 classes.
description: Exploit, building on E007's finding that time scales with pixel count. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, use a more aggressive resolution schedule: the first 30% of steps at 20 px, then 30% at 24 px, 20% at 28 px, and the last 20% at 32 px. Each resolution is compiled and warmed up in build with channels_last synthetic batches of the exact training shape. Use error_on_recompile after build. Keep the global max-pool head so the network works at every size.

expected: Time falls 4-7% (about 0.3-0.5 s). Accuracy changes by -0.1 to -0.4 pp. A loss under 0.3 pp supports H1.5.2 and gives a cheaper per-epoch base that can be stacked with the epoch trim.
description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe, narrow only the last residual group from 576 to 512 channels (the airbench96_faster width). Keep everything else the same, including the Muon lr, epochs and resizing schedule. Re-warm-up all compiled shapes in build.
note: committee: most disputed (info 0.95), +1 priority

expected: The 10-seed mean is within 0.3 pp of the 3-seed mean, and per-seed std is 0.15-0.4 pp. If the 10-seed mean is more than 0.2 pp below the 3-seed mean, the safe margin above 0.753 must rise, which limits further epoch cuts. Epoch 1 is expected to be under 0.3 s slower than later epochs (H3.3.1 refuted).
description: Diagnostic, settling the committee's std and 40-seed cruxes (W2, W3). Run the current best recipe (E007, or the 8.5-epoch trim if it is kept) offline on held-out seeds 3-12 with the same harness code path, without editing the recipe. Record per-seed accuracy, the mean, the std and the offset from the seeds 0-2 mean. Also record per-epoch CUDA-event times to settle H3.3.1 (first-epoch overhead) in the same pass.
note: ideate: Rewritten as a new idea that runs the held-out-seed diagnostic on the current tip, E010 (I013 still pointed at E007 or E008, which are no longer the tip). The margin crux that all four members raised now concerns E010's 0.18 pp margin.

expected: Time falls 2-6% (0.15-0.4 s), because the 4-CPU pin makes launch overhead visible at about 25 steps per epoch with many small optimizer kernels. Per-seed accuracy should be bit-identical or within 0.05 pp. Any recompile or capture inside train shows up as a time rise of more than 1 s and must be checked with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles first.
description: Explore. On the E007 recipe, capture the train step (forward, backward, Muon Newton-Schulz plus SGD update, and the EMA update on steps where it applies) in CUDA graphs. Use torch.compile mode='max-autotune' (cudagraphs on) or a manual torch.cuda.graph per resolution with static input buffers that the GPU augmentation writes into. Capture every resolution in build on synthetic data. Math stays identical.
note: committee: most disputed (info 0.95), +1 priority

description: Explore. On the E007 recipe, after the final EMA/Lookahead weights are copied in at the end of train, reset the BatchNorm running statistics and recompute them with one no-grad forward pass in train mode (momentum=None, cumulative average) over 5k training images at 32 px, inside the timed train. No parameter updates are made, and eval stays a plain forward pass.
note: committee veto: 3/4 members forecast clear harm, none an improvement

expected: Time is unchanged at about 6.6 s. The 10-seed mean is within 0.3 pp of 0.7548 and per-seed std is 0.15-0.35 pp. If the held-out mean is under 0.751, the tip is fragile for the 40-seed judgment. description: Diagnostic that sharpens I013 for the current tip; it makes no recipe change. Record per-seed accuracy, the 10-seed mean, the std and the offset from the seeds 0-2 mean (0.7548). In the same pass, record per-epoch CUDA-event times to settle H3.3.1. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

expected: Time is unchanged (±1%, about 6.64 s). Accuracy moves between -0.3 and +0.4 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.3.1 and buys about 0.5 epoch for the next trim. A loss would show that strong LS is still needed for a 100-way head in a short run, and the next test should try LS 0.35.
description: Exploit, as a near-free accuracy lever (W1 and W3 crux). On the E010 recipe, change only the label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 (the airbench96_faster value) in the training loss. Epochs, resizing, Muon/SGD settings and Lookahead/EMA stay the same, and so do the compiled shapes. Since the loss changes only by a constant, no extra warm-up is needed beyond the usual error_on_recompile check.

expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.4 and +0.4 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.5.1, and the run after it should try ×2. A loss of 0.2 pp or more points the next test at ×0.67.
description: Exploit. On the E010 recipe, change only the Muon learning rate for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5). The SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head), momentum 0.6, batch size 2000, schedule shape, epochs and Lookahead/EMA stay the same. The 0.24 value comes from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon, and E006's surprise gain (+0.66 pp, outside every member's range) suggests the CIFAR-100 optimum has not been explored.

expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.4 and +0.3 pp. A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.5.1. A loss of more than 0.2 pp shows that wd is part of what makes the solution sharp, so the next test should try wd ×1.5.
description: Exploit, as the second point of the coarse grid. On the E010 recipe, halve only the weight decay for all parameter groups (Muon conv filters and SGD groups), keeping the same decoupled or coupled form the code uses now. Everything else stays identical. Short runs with EMA may need less regularization than the 0.012 CIFAR-10 value.

expected: Time falls 1.5-3% (0.1-0.2 s, to about 6.45-6.55 s). Accuracy changes between -0.25 and +0.05 pp. The idea pays off if the loss is under 0.1 pp, which is a better rate than the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp). A loss above 0.2 pp means orthogonalization quality matters for CIFAR-100, and NS should stay at 5 steps.
description: Exploit on cost per step. Muon added 0.35 s (+3.8%) in E006. On the E010 recipe, cut the Newton-Schulz iterations in the Muon update from 5 to 3, keeping the same quintic coefficients and bf16. Everything else stays the same. Re-warm-up the compiled optimizer step in build, with error_on_recompile.
note: Premise wrong: the Muon update already uses 3 Newton-Schulz iterations (newton_schulz(steps=3), as in airbench94_muon), not 5. Also E011/E012 show fixed per-step overhead (Muon+optimizer+launch) is only ~5% of train time, so NS 3->2 could save <1%.

expected: Accuracy is bit-identical per seed. If explain finds at least one break or sync, time falls 2-5% (about 0.15-0.3 s). If it finds none, change the code anyway only if the profile shows GPU idle above 5%; otherwise record H2.2.3 as refuted and lower I014's priority (CUDA graphs would then have little to gain).
description: Explore, settling the W2/W4 crux about launch versus compute. Run torch._dynamo.explain and a short torch.profiler trace offline on the E010 train step on synthetic data: GPU augmentation, forward/backward, Muon+SGD step, Lookahead/EMA update and LR schedule. If there are graph breaks or host syncs (for example .item(), Python-scalar LR, or tensor-to-bool checks), remove them: keep LR as a GPU tensor, fold augmentation into the compiled region, and keep the math identical. Commit only the break-free version and record the measured GPU idle fraction in the notebook.

expected: Time is unchanged within 1%. Accuracy lands within ±0.3 pp of 0.7548. A drop of more than 0.3 pp means the Lookahead pull-back trajectory, not endpoint averaging, drives the gain (refuting H1.3.5). A gain would suggest that longer averaging horizons are worth tuning next.
description: Explore, aimed at the E005 counterexample (endpoint averaging was worth about 1 pp, far more than forecast). On the E010 recipe, replace the airbench96_faster Lookahead, which resets the fast weights to the slow weights every 5 steps, with a plain EMA of weights and BN buffers. The EMA updates every 5 steps with the same alpha ramp, never writes back into the fast weights, and is copied into the model only at the end of train. Create and reset all EMA state in prepare.
note: ideate: Time-neutral mechanism test with no route to a better score: the committee agrees (conflict 0, 1/5 improve votes) that plain EMA will land at or below the Lookahead tip. Even if it matched, nothing gets faster.

expected: Time falls about 8% (2.7 epochs move from about 0.71 to 0.51 s/epoch, saving about 0.5 s), to about 6.0-6.15 s. Accuracy changes by -0.1 to -0.5 pp, to about 0.753-0.756. A loss of 0.3 pp or less beats the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp) and supports the tail-sets-accuracy reading of E011. A loss above 0.5 pp means the middle phase matters too, so resizing should stop here.
description: Exploit. Tests a proposed new child of H2.3: accuracy is set mainly in the final 32 px phase, so the 28 px middle phase can be dropped cheaply. On the E015 recipe (Muon, Lookahead/EMA, CUDA graphs, 9 epochs, last group 512), change only the resolution schedule from 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps to 24/32 px at 70/30% of steps. The 32 px tail keeps exactly its current step count and position, so the LR and EMA schedules stay the same. Build no longer needs the 28 px graph; keep the 24 and 32 px warm-up and capture, and keep error_on_recompile on after build.

expected: Time falls about 5.5-6% (about 0.38 s), to about 6.2 s. That is the same saving as a uniform 0.5-epoch trim, which E008 showed costs about 0.18-0.27 pp. If accuracy is set in the tail, the loss is 0.15 pp or less (about 0.755-0.757). A loss of 0.25 pp or more means early epochs count as much as late ones, and plain uniform trims are the right dial.
description: Exploit, testing W5's crux (is accuracy set in the 32 px phase?) against a uniform epoch trim. On the E015 recipe, cut 0.75 epoch from the 24 px phase only: 3.6 → 2.85 epochs at 24 px, with the 28 px (2.7 epochs) and 32 px (2.7 epochs) phases unchanged in absolute length. Total is 8.25 epochs. Stretch the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules to the new total step count, as in E008. Compiled shapes are unchanged; error_on_recompile stays on. If I-swap (24/32 only) is kept first, apply the same 0.75-epoch cut to its 24 px phase instead.
note: ideate: Superseded. The tail-sets-accuracy crux is tested more cleanly and with a larger time saving by the 24/32 swap, and the epoch dial by the uniform 1.0-epoch trim (H4.2.4) on E016. The 24 px-only cut can come back after the swap result.

expected: Time is unchanged at about 6.58 s (±1%). If autotune is stable, seeds 0-2 are bit-identical across rebuilds. (1) Rebuild E015 from scratch (fresh inductor cache) and run it twice through ar.py. Check that max-autotune with cudagraphs reselects the same kernels, giving bit-identical per-seed accuracies on seeds 0-2. (2) Run the same build offline on held-out seeds 3-12 through the harness code path (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Record the per-seed accuracies, mean, std and the offset from 0.7574. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

The margin over 0.753 after E015/E016 is real at ~+0.3-0.5 pp population-level; seeds 0-2 means deviate from held-out by up to +-0.4 pp, so E015's 0.7574 was partly luck. Kernel reselection on rebuild doesn't change this conclusion.

expected: Time rises 2-5% (per-step fixed cost is about 1.4 ms × 135 extra steps, plus slightly lower kernel efficiency), to about 6.7-6.9 s. Accuracy rises 0.1-0.6 pp. The idea pays off only with a gain of at least 0.35 pp, which buys about 0.75 epoch (7%) in the next trim. A gain under 0.2 pp means bs 2000 is fine; discard.

On the E015 recipe, change only the batch size from 2000 to 1250 (40 steps per epoch exactly, so no ragged batch; 360 steps instead of 225). Keep the per-step Muon lr at 0.24 and momentum at 0.6; E014 showed the lr is flat over 0.24-0.36, so the extra steps' larger total movement is tolerated. Scale the SGD-group lrs with batch size the way the code already does. Express the resizing and EMA/Lookahead schedules as fractions of total steps. Recapture every resolution's CUDA graph at the new batch shape in build, with error_on_recompile.

expected: Time is unchanged (±1%). Accuracy moves between -0.3 and +0.4 pp. A gain of at least 0.3 pp supports H1.5.1 and funds about 0.75 epoch. A loss of 0.2 pp or more means 0.6 is near-optimal or high, and the grid should stop.
description: Exploit, the third point of the optimizer grid (LS and lr were flat). On the E015 recipe, change only the Muon momentum for the conv filters from 0.6 to 0.8 (still Nesterov). The SGD groups, lr, wd, batch size, schedules, epochs and Lookahead/EMA stay the same. Since momentum is a Python constant baked into the graph, recapture every resolution in build.
note: ideate: All committee members forecast no effect (0/4 improve votes), and the Muon scalar knobs (lr, LS) have been flat within noise. Low information, low expected gain.

expected: Time falls 8-12% (to about 5.8-6.05 s). Accuracy falls 0.3-0.8 pp, so the run is likely infeasible on its own. The exchange rate decides the outcome: 2.5 s/pp or better (for example 0.6 s for 0.25 pp) beats the epoch dial (about 1.9 s/pp), and the narrower net should then be paired with an accuracy booster or a +0.25-epoch top-up. On the E015 recipe, narrow only group 2 from 384 to 320 channels. Keep group 1 (128) and group 3 (512), the Muon lr, epochs, the resizing schedule and Lookahead/EMA unchanged. Recapture all shapes in build.

description: Explore/exploit on the biggest FLOP block. This replaces I028, rebased on E016. On the E016 recipe, cut weight decay to ×0.25 of the original on the SGD groups only (BN biases, whitening bias, head), leaving the Muon conv-filter wd at E016's ×0.5. First check in code whether the filters are renormalized; if they are, filter wd is inert and this is equivalent to a global cut. Nothing else changes. Recapture the graphs if wd is baked in as a constant.

expected: About 7% fewer conv MACs plus less memory-bound elementwise work, so time falls 5-9%, to about 6.0-6.25 s. Accuracy falls 0.15-0.6 pp. A rate of 1.9 s/pp or better supports H2.5.2 and makes this a cheaper cut than group-2 width. A loss above 0.5 pp means early depth matters for 100 classes.
description: Explore a second FLOP lever with a different mechanism: depth at the highest-resolution stage. On the E016 recipe, remove only the third conv (128→128, with its BN-GELU) in group 1, keeping the residual and pooling structure otherwise intact. Group 1's maps are the largest, so its elementwise BN/GELU traffic is also the most memory-bound. Widths, optimizer, schedules, epochs and EMA stay unchanged. Recapture all resolutions in build, with error_on_recompile on.
note: ideate: All four committee members forecast no improvement and none forecast harm. They agree that removing about 7% of MACs returns only about 5–7% of time, as in E021's efficiency loss, while costing at least 0.3 pp. H2.5 evidence (E010 at 1.4 s/pp, E021 at 1.0 s/pp) shows width and depth cuts trade worse than the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). Low expected value; the H2.2.4 profiling idea gets at the underlying question (where architecture time goes) more cheaply.

expected: Pixel-weighted cost falls about 3.5%. E011 ran slightly faster than proportional, so time falls 3.5-5%, to about 6.25-6.35 s. Accuracy changes by -0.05 to -0.35 pp. A loss of 0.2 pp or less with time down at least 4% supports H2.3.2 and pins E011's cliff on the shortened 32 px tail, not on the 20 px phase. A loss above 0.35 pp means 20 px itself is harmful on 100 classes.
description: Explore. This is the single-factor version of E011, separating its two confounded changes. On the E016 recipe, change only the first phase: the first 15% of steps run at 20 px, followed by 24 px for 25%, 28 px for 30% and 32 px for 30%. The 32 px tail keeps its exact step count and position, and the LR and EMA schedules are unchanged. Warm up and capture the 20 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, with error_on_recompile on.

expected: Time falls about 5% (about 0.33 s), to about 6.2 s. Held-out 10-seed mean falls 0.1–0.3 pp from E017's 0.7577, to about 0.755–0.757. Seeds 0–2 land at 0.751–0.758, roughly a 70% chance of clearing 0.753. If I033 was kept with at least +0.2 pp held-out, add that much to every accuracy figure. A held-out mean of at least 0.7545 supports H4.2.4 and makes this the new tip if seeds 0–2 clear the bar. A held-out mean below 0.754 means the dial is steeper near 9 epochs and further time must come from resolution.
description: Exploit: test the untested −0.5 point of the epoch dial. Apply it to the current tip: E017, or I033's recipe if I033 is kept. Cut 0.5 true epoch uniformly, for example about 9.5 → 9.0 true epochs; read the exact step count from the code first (H4.2.3). Resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share). The LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. Changing the step count also changes RNG consumption, so seeds 0–2 get re-rolled. So in the same session, run the recipe offline on held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Base keep or discard on both numbers, not on the 3-seed mean alone. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds-0–2 draw.

expected: Time falls 3.5–4.5% (about 0.25–0.29 s, since the 28 px phase runs about 2.85 epochs at about 0.71 → 0.61 s/epoch), to about 6.27 s. If the regime matters, the held-out mean falls by 0.15 pp or less, a rate of about 2 s/pp or better, which beats the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). If pixel count matters (E018's rate pro-rated), it falls about 0.3–0.35 pp, and resizing should stop at 24/28/32.
description: Explore W5's crux (proposed H2.3 child): the accuracy cost of the low-res phases depends on the final feature-map regime (3×3 vs 2×2 after group 3), not on pixel count. Feature-map sizes: 32→31/15/7/3, 28→27/13/6/3, 26→25/12/6/3, 24→23/11/5/2. E018 replaced the 28 px phase (3×3 regime) with 24 px (2×2 regime) and lost 0.68 pp. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the middle phase from 28 px to 26 px, keeping the 40/30/30% step split. The 26 px phase stays in the 3×3 regime with about 14% fewer pixels. Warm up and capture the 26 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, and keep error_on_recompile on. Judge accuracy on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as on seeds 0–2.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves between −0.2 and +0.35 pp from E017's 0.7577. A held-out gain of at least 0.2 pp supports the child and funds about 0.5 epoch more of trimming. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means mid-run pull-back slows feature learning, so the next point to test is exponent 4.
description: Exploit, as a time-neutral accuracy booster to fund trims (W1 crux: does a stronger or longer EMA add 0.3 pp?). E005 showed end-of-run averaging is worth about 1 pp on CIFAR-100, and E009 showed a lower final LR adds nothing on top of it, so averaging strength is the untuned part. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the Lookahead alpha ramp exponent from 3 to 2: alpha = 0.95**5 * (step/total)**2 instead of **3. The averaging then pulls harder from about mid-run on. Update frequency (every 5 steps), the final full copy, LR schedule, epochs and resolution all stay unchanged. Alpha is a per-step tensor or constant, so recapture the graphs if it is baked in. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. This proposes a new H1.3 child: the airbench96 averaging schedule is under-tuned for CIFAR-100 short runs.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp. Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 (E013), so a gain of at least 0.2 pp would point to a size-specific effect and support H2.3.4. A gain of at least 0.2 pp would also suggest pairing it with I035's 20 px phase. A change within ±0.1 pp refutes H2.3.4 as a lever here.
description: Explore the EfficientNetV2 mechanism (D002, C0019/C0020): regularization should scale with image size. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the label smoothing per phase: LS 0.15 during the 24 px and 28 px phases (70% of steps) and LS 0.3 in the 32 px tail. Crop, flip, epochs and schedules stay unchanged. LS is a per-phase constant, so it can sit in each resolution's captured graph or be passed as a GPU scalar; check for recompiles with error_on_recompile. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: ideate: All four members forecast harm and none an improvement. Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 (E013). The EfficientNetV2 size-dependent regularization effect relies on large regularization ranges, not LS 0.15 vs 0.3 in a 9-epoch run, so a 0.2 pp gain is unlikely and would not change time.

expected: No change to time or accuracy. Expected: overall about 80–110 TFLOP/s at 32 px. Group-3 convs at 2–3 px maps and BN/GELU elementwise work are expected to be the least efficient, roughly 10–20% of step time combined. If one layer's share far exceeds its FLOP share, a targeted fix (fusing BN-GELU into the conv epilogue, padding channels or maps to tile sizes) becomes a lossless 3–8% lever. If every conv runs at least 80% of the median, H2.2.4 is supported and only epoch/resolution/accuracy levers remain.
description: Diagnostic, making no recipe change. It answers W1's crux on why group 2 at 320 channels returned only half its MAC savings (E021), which sets the payoff of every architecture lever. Offline, run torch.profiler on the E017 train step on synthetic data at each resolution (24/28/32 px, batch 2000), forward and backward. Record per-kernel GPU time for each conv layer and for the non-conv work (BN/GELU, pooling, Muon NS, Lookahead), and the achieved TFLOP/s per conv. Flag any layer below 50% of the median conv efficiency (candidates: group-3 convs on 2×2/3×3 maps, the whitening conv, the 128-channel group-1 convs) and any non-conv share above 10%. Do not edit submissions/arena/. Write per-layer efficiencies to the notebook.
note: ideate: Low information: all four members forecast the same outcome (at least 90 TFLOP/s at 32 px, no kernel lever over 5%), and the diagnostic changes no recipe. Its main use was interpreting architecture cuts, and E021/E024 already gave the tile-alignment lesson. I043's measured time saving will answer the group-1 backward cost question directly.

expected: Proxy cost adds about 8–15% time per main step. The gain has to come from accuracy per step: the run is worth keeping only if accuracy rises at least 0.6 pp (about 1.5 epochs' worth) at roughly equal time, so that it can then be traded for epochs. Likely outcome: time +8–12% (about 7.1–7.3 s) and accuracy −0.3 to +0.6 pp. A held-out gain of 0.4 pp or less refutes H2.4.1 for CIFAR-100, where hard examples are noisier than on CIFAR-10.
description: Explore, the one unexplored large lever (H2.4, from airbench96_faster). On the E017 recipe, add proxy-based hard-example selection. A small proxy net (same stem; widths 32/64/64, one conv per group) trains alongside the main net on full batches. Each main-net step uses the top-50% highest-proxy-loss samples of a 4000-image candidate batch (so the main batch stays at 2000). Raise the total candidate epochs so the main net's step count matches E017's. Proxy state, its optimizer and RNG are all created and reset in prepare, and the proxy forward plus topk are captured in the compiled step. Warm up every resolution in build. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: committee veto: 4/4 members forecast clear harm, none an improvement

expected: Branch (b): time falls about 2.7% (about 0.17 s), from 6.20 to about 6.03 s. Held-out mean falls 0.05–0.2 pp (dial: 0.44 pp per epoch), from 0.7556 to about 0.7545. Seeds 0–2 land at 0.751–0.758, about a 70% chance of clearing 0.753. Branch (a): time about 5.86 s, held-out about 0.7533 plus I038's gain. A held-out drop of more than 0.25 pp per 0.25 epoch means the dial steepens below 9 epochs.
description: Exploit: spend the margin on the epoch dial, with a branch that depends on I038, which is still running. Base: the current tip E023 (9.0 true epochs), or I038's recipe if I038 is kept. Branch (a): if I038 is kept with a held-out seeds 3–12 gain of at least 0.15 pp, cut 0.5 true epoch to 8.5 true epochs (212 steps at batch 2000). This is E020's step count plus I038's averaging. Branch (b): otherwise, cut 0.25 true epoch to 8.75 true epochs (219 steps). In both branches the resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share), and the LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020/E023. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. The step count changes RNG use, so in the same session also run held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean is at least 0.7535. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds 0–2 draw.

expected: Time falls 4–6% (about 0.25–0.35 s), to about 5.85–5.95 s. Held-out mean falls 0.05–0.3 pp from 0.7556. The deciding number is the exchange rate. Better than 1.5 s/pp (e.g. 0.3 s for 0.2 pp or less) beats the epoch dial and supports H2.6.1, and the next step tests freezing at 65%. If time falls under 3%, the backward through group 1 is not the cost the MAC model says it is (feed this into I040/H6). A loss above 0.35 pp means early layers keep learning usefully at the end of short CIFAR-100 runs.
description: Explore/exploit: a FreezeOut-style backward truncation, a mechanism not yet tried in this loop. On the E023 tip, put group-1 conv filters (Muon) and the whitening bias plus group-1 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR schedule follows the global triangle up to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. The other groups keep their schedules. For the last 25% of steps, all of them at 32 px, detach group 1's output before group 2, and use a second compiled train step that does no group-1 or whitening backward and leaves group-1 params out of the Muon/SGD update. Group-1 BN still runs in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture both 32 px step variants (full and truncated) in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Back-of-envelope: group 1 is about 20% of conv MACs at the largest maps, so skipping its weight-grad and input-grad work saves about 14–18% of a 32 px step (including memory-bound BN/GELU backward), applied to about 2.0 s of tail time. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: Time falls 8–10% (about 0.5–0.6 s), to about 5.6–5.7 s. A uniform cut of the same steps on the epoch dial would cost about 0.35 pp (held-out about 0.752). Selection is worth keeping if the held-out mean drops 0.2 pp or less (to 0.7536 or higher), so it beats the dial at better than 2.5 s/pp. A drop of 0.35 pp or more means easy examples still carry signal in 9-epoch CIFAR-100 runs (or that stale losses pick noisy or ambiguous images), which would refute this child.
description: Explore: proposes a new H2.4 child. Drop easy examples using free per-sample losses from the main net, with no proxy. The committee vetoed I041 for the proxy's cost; this version adds no extra forward passes. On the E023 tip, change the compiled train step to return the per-sample loss (reduction='none', then mean for backward) and scatter it into a GPU loss buffer indexed by sample id. The buffer is created and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 onward, each epoch's shuffled order uses only the 90% of samples with the highest loss in the previous pass (torch.topk on the GPU, then the usual GPU shuffle). The batch stays at 2000 and the ragged remainder is dropped. Total steps fall from 225 to about 205 (1 + 8×0.9 epoch-equivalents). The resolution phases (40/30/30), LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules are fractions of the new total step count. Alternating flip still uses each sample's own pass parity. Warm up the modified step in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: Time falls 1–3% (fixed per-step overhead is about 5% of train time, plus better GPU use at 24 px), to about 6.0–6.15 s. Held-out mean moves −0.35 to +0.1 pp, median about −0.1. A loss of 0.1 pp or less with at least 1.5% time saved supports H5.1.1, Muon's large critical batch. A loss of 0.25 pp or more means step count matters even under Muon, which closes the batch lever.
description: Exploit, the time-favorable direction of H5 (the committee vetoed I026's smaller batch as clear harm). On the E023 tip at the same true epoch count (9.0), raise batch from 2000 to 2500, which gives exactly 20 steps per epoch, 180 steps instead of 225. Scale the SGD-group (BN, whitening bias, head) lr linearly with batch the way the code does now, and leave Muon lr at 0.24 and momentum at 0.6. Express the resolution, LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules as fractions of the new step count, keeping the 5-step Lookahead period. Recapture every resolution's graph at batch 2500 in build, with error_on_recompile on. Check peak memory at 32 px. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: ideate: The committee agrees (conflict 0): the step is GPU-bound, so batch 2500 saves only about 2%, while 20% fewer Muon and Lookahead steps in a short run likely costs at least 0.15 pp. That is no better than the epoch dial, and the tip's population margin (held-out 0.7526) cannot absorb a loss. The low-information outcome isn't worth a slot.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.25 to +0.3 pp from 0.7556, median about +0.05. A held-out gain of at least 0.2 pp supports H1.5.6 and funds about 0.5 epoch of trimming (pair it with the epoch-trim idea). A loss of at least 0.15 pp puts the optimum at 0.24–0.36 and ends the Muon lr grid.
description: Exploit, a time-neutral booster to fund trims. On the E023 tip, double only the Muon lr for conv filters from 0.24 to 0.48. The SGD groups, momentum 0.6, wd ×0.5, batch, schedules, epochs, resolution and Lookahead/EMA all stay the same. E014 (×1.5 at the old wd) moved +0.09 pp. The wd ×0.5 base and E006's large unexplained Muon gain leave the upper side of the lr range untested. If lr is baked into the graph as a constant, recapture the graphs. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2, since a single 3-seed difference under 0.4 pp is unreadable.
note: ideate: All four committee members forecast harm and none an improvement. Muon lr was flat between 0.24 and 0.36 (E014), and the change is time-neutral, so a gain would have to be ≥0.2 pp, beyond the forecast range. It also targets E023, which is no longer the tip.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%, about 5.88 s). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp from 0.7526, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.6.1 and funds about 0.35 epoch or the 20 px extension (H2.3.6). A loss of at least 0.15 pp means the warm-up protects the Muon/BN-bias start in short runs, and the next point should be a later peak, not an earlier one.
description: Exploit, a time-neutral accuracy booster. The tip's population mean is now below the bar (held-out 0.7526), so the next time cut needs one first. On the E027 tip (8.75 true epochs, 219 steps at batch 2000, 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%), change only the LR warm-up length. First read the current warm-up and peak fraction from the code (airbench96 uses a peak at about 0.23 of steps). Halve it so the peak comes earlier, with the same peak value and a linear decay to the same 0.07 floor, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups. The Lookahead/EMA ramp, resolution phases, epochs, wd and LS all stay unchanged. If LR is a GPU tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every resolution in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if the held-out gain is at least 0.15 pp and seeds 0–2 clear 0.753.

expected: Time unchanged or −0.3% (half as many Lookahead updates). Held-out mean moves −0.2 to +0.25 pp from 0.7526, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.3.7 (fast weights need longer free runs), and the next point is every 20 steps. A loss of at least 0.15 pp means frequent pull-back is part of the gain, consistent with Switch-EMA, and closes H1.3's tuning branch.
description: Exploit, a time-neutral averaging booster in the direction opposite to E025 (which pulled harder and hurt by 0.27 pp held-out). D003 (C0024/C0025) points to the reset interval as the untuned Lookahead knob. On the E027 tip, change only the Lookahead update interval from every 5 to every 10 steps. Rescale the per-update retention so the total pull per step is unchanged (alpha_10 = alpha_5**2 at each ramp point, same exponent 3), and keep the final full copy. LR, epochs, resolution, wd and LS stay unchanged. Recapture the step graphs if the interval or alpha is baked in, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.2 to +0.25 pp from 0.7526, median 0. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.3.8: late LS removal sharpens the 100-way head once features have formed. A loss of at least 0.15 pp means LS acts as end-point regularization that the Lookahead average relies on, and LS tuning should stop. (Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 in E013, so a phase-specific effect is the only remaining LS question.)
description: Exploit, a time-neutral booster that targets the end-point, where averaging forms (E005 showed the late phase is worth about 1 pp). On the E027 tip, keep label smoothing at 0.3 for the first 85% of steps and set it to 0 for the final 15%, which lies entirely inside the 32 px phase. Pass LS as a GPU scalar into the compiled loss, or capture a second 32 px step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: About 1.3 true epochs move from about 0.51 to about 0.36 s/epoch, so time falls 3–3.5% (about 0.18–0.2 s), to about 5.68–5.72 s. If early resolution is free, the held-out mean drops 0.1 pp or less, a rate of at least 2 s/pp, which beats the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). If it repeats E026's rate (about 1.2 s/pp), it drops about 0.15 pp, which is no better than epochs. Then stop resizing and spend future time cuts on epochs.
description: Exploit and crux test (W1/W5: is early low resolution close to free?). Run it on the E027 tip, or on the tip plus any booster above that was kept with at least +0.15 pp held-out. Change only the resolution split from 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30% of steps to 30/10/30/30%. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions, and the LR and Lookahead schedules are unchanged. The 20 px graph is already captured in build, and error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean stays at or above 0.752 (the 40-seed official bar of 0.75 then has at least 0.2 pp of headroom).

expected: Time +0.5–1% (three extra 12×12 eigendecompositions and patch extraction in prepare). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.2 pp supports the stem-mismatch child and suggests resolution cuts can go further once the stem is matched. A change within ±0.1 pp refutes it, which leaves (a) the peak-LR timing or (c) the tail length as the mechanisms behind H2.3's cost.
description: Explore (W5 crux, a proposed new H2.3 child: the low-res cost is partly a stem-statistics mismatch). The frozen 2×2 patch-whitening conv is computed in prepare from 32 px patches. Downsampled 20/24/28 px images have higher per-pixel frequency content, so the frozen filter leaves their outputs non-white, and BN plus group 1 must re-adapt at every resolution jump. On the E027 tip, compute the whitening eigenbasis in prepare separately for each training resolution (from at most 5k training images resized with the same F.interpolate path, inside timed prepare). Use the matching frozen whitening weights in each phase. The 32 px weights stay the ones used at eval. The whitening bias is shared, and nothing else changes. Capture each resolution's graph in build with its own whitening buffer, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: ideate: The committee gives it 0/4 improve votes, a median of about +0.05 pp (flat) and +0.5–1% time. It cannot produce a time win, and a gain of ≥0.2 pp is outside every member's range. Low expected improvement and low information.

expected: Time about 5.65–5.75 s (E028's 5.36 s plus about 0.3–0.35 s for 0.5 epoch, part of it in cheap frozen steps), which beats E027 (5.88 s) by 2–4%. Held-out mean about 0.7540–0.7555 (E028's 0.7525 plus 0.5 epoch × 0.37–0.44 pp/epoch). Seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 with about 60–75% probability. If held-out is below 0.7535, the freeze has a hidden cost at the longer schedule; then try 9.5 epochs only if it still projects under 5.85 s.
description: Exploit: stack the free lever (the freeze) with the cheapest accuracy booster (epochs). Start from the E027 tip and apply E028's freeze exactly as committed in fcacfc6. Group-1 conv filters, the whitening bias and group-1 BN params get their own param groups. Their LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. For the last 25% of steps, use the truncated compiled 32 px step: group-1 output detached, and no group-1 or whitening backward or update. Group-1 BN stays in train mode and Lookahead averages every param. Then change only the step count: 8.75 to 9.25 true epochs (about 231 steps at batch 2000). Read the exact count from the code. The resolution phases (20/24/28/32 at 15/25/30/30%), the freeze point (75%), and the LR and Lookahead schedules stay fixed fractions of the new total. Capture full and truncated 32 px variants in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. In the same session, run held-out seeds 3–12. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase seeds 0–2.

expected: Per-seed accuracies bit-identical to the base (to be verified, which settles W5's crux). Mean time falls 0.03–0.10 s (prepare mean about 0.11 to about 0.04–0.06 s, mostly trial 0), i.e. 0.5–1.5%. If the tensors can't be made bit-identical, report that and fall back to a held-out-judged version.
description: Exploit and crux test (W5: does a math-identical change keep the tip's per-seed outcomes?). Base: the current tip (E027, or the H2.6.2 successor if kept). Change only systems work in prepare, keeping every number bit-identical. (1) Move the training images to the GPU as uint8 and do the float conversion, normalization and channels_last/fp16 cast on the GPU, in the same op order and dtype the CPU path uses now. (2) In build, run prepare's GPU kernels once on synthetic uint8 tensors of the real shape: the whitening patch extraction and eigendecomposition, the normalization and the allocations. This removes trial 0's 0.21 s first-call cost. The whitening is still computed from the same images as now; do not subsample. Before launching, check offline with torch.equal that the normalized train tensor and the whitening weights equal the current ones. If they don't, adjust the op order until they do, or abandon. Record per-trial prepare time.

expected: Time falls 1–3% (about 0.06–0.15 s). It removes only the stem's input-grad and the bias-grad reduction on the largest maps between 20% and 75% of steps. Held-out mean within ±0.1 pp of the base. A loss above 0.15 pp means the bias keeps adapting to resolution switches; the 20/24/28 px phases happen after 20%.
description: Exploit. First read the code. If the whitening bias already stops training before 25% of steps, close H2.6.3 without a run. Otherwise, on the H2.6.2 successor (or E027 if it is not kept), stop the whitening bias's gradient after 20% of steps (Hiverge; airbench96 trains it for 3/45 epochs). Use a third compiled step variant in which the whitening output is detached, so no input-grad of group 1's first conv and no whitening backward on the 31×31 maps. Group 1 still trains normally until the freeze. Anneal the whitening-bias LR to 0 by 20% of steps. Capture the new variant at every resolution it runs at (20/24/28/32 px) in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: Time falls 3–5% (about 0.17–0.25 s, about 33 more truncated steps at about 7–9.5 ms each), to about 5.45–5.55 s. Held-out mean falls 0–0.2 pp. A loss of 0.15 pp or less beats the epoch dial (about 1.5–2.7 s/pp) and supports H2.6.4. A loss above 0.25 pp means group 1 still learns usefully at 60–75% of a 9-epoch CIFAR-100 run, and the freeze stays at 75%.
description: Exploit, the freeze dose. Run only once the H2.6.2 successor is kept, and on it. Move the group-1 and whitening-bias freeze start from 75% to 60% of steps. The group-1 LR is annealed to 0 by 60%. Everything else is unchanged, including the step count, resolution phases and LR/Lookahead schedules. The truncated step now also runs during the last 10% of the 28 px phase (60–70%), so capture a truncated 28 px variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep if held-out ≥ 0.7545 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753, or if the held-out loss is ≤ 0.1 pp and a follow-up epoch top-up is planned.

expected: Time unchanged. The fresh mean is within 0.15 pp of the seeds 3–12 mean (expected offset about −0.05 pp from selection). Pooled 20-seed mean ≥ 0.753 supports H4.3.2, and the candidate has about 0.3 pp of headroom over the 40-seed bar of 0.75. If the fresh mean is below 0.752, further time cuts must stop until accuracy is bought back.
description: Validation diagnostic, with no recipe change. Run it immediately after a candidate tip is kept (the H2.6.2 successor, or whatever is the tip once H2.6.3/H3.2.1 are stacked). Seeds 3–12 have driven about 10 keep decisions and carry a winner's curse. Run the committed recipe offline on fresh seeds 13–22 through the harness (benchmark.run --seed 13 --n 10). Record per-seed accuracy, mean and std, and the pooled 20-seed mean with its SE. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

expected: Time falls 1.5–3% (about 0.08–0.15 s) beyond the base. The 3 BN reductions and normalizations on 128×31×31 maps go away from about 55 frozen steps. Held-out within ±0.15 pp: eval-mode BN removes batch-stat noise in the frozen layers, which may even help slightly. A saving under 1% refutes H2.6.5 and says the frozen forward is conv-bound, not BN-bound.
description: Explore, the next memory-bound lever on the frozen stem. On the H2.6.2 successor (or the freeze recipe in fcacfc6), at the freeze point: run one no-grad train-mode forward of group 1 over the current batch to set its BN running stats. Use the existing buffers if their values are already the frozen-phase stats. Then, for the frozen phase, put group-1 BN in eval mode and fold scale and shift into the conv weights and biases (done inside timed train, once). The truncated step then runs group 1 as conv+bias+GELU under no_grad, with no BN statistics reductions on the 31×31 maps. Lookahead still averages the unfolded params. Keep the unfolded copies so the final weights and BN buffers stay consistent: either fold only in the compiled frozen forward, or unfold before the final copy. Eval uses the standard model. Capture the new truncated variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.

expected: No change to time or accuracy. Predicted: non-GEMM kernels take ≥30% of the 32 px full step. Whitening plus group 1 take ≥35% of it, against about 20% of MACs. Group-3 convs run below 70 TFLOP/s. If non-GEMM is under 20%, H6.3 is refuted and H2.6.5 drops to priority 1.
description: Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It sets the value of the remaining stem levers (H2.6.4/H2.6.5/H2.6.3) and the PCIe-transfer caveat in H4.3. Offline, run torch.profiler on the tip's compiled 32 px full step and truncated step, and on the 24 px step, with batch 2000 and synthetic channels_last data. Record GPU time by kernel class (conv GEMM fwd/dgrad/wgrad, BN, GELU, pool, elementwise, Muon NS, Lookahead) and by layer group (whitening, group 1, 2, 3, head). Also record achieved conv TFLOP/s per group. Write the table to the notebook and label each kept lever as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. Do not edit submissions/arena/.

expected: Time falls about 2–4% (the NS overhead, about 0.15–0.2 s). Held-out mean falls 0.2–0.6 pp (median about −0.35), which would support H1.2.2 and confirm Muon as an accuracy source worth more than its time. A loss of 0.15 pp or less means E006's gain came from batch size or the re-draw, so dropping Muon is a free 3% cut. That would also reopen batch tuning under SGD (H5).
description: Explore. E006's +0.66 pp confounded Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw. On the current tip (the H2.6.2 successor if kept, else E027), replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (momentum 0.9, as in the E005 recipe). Scale the conv-filter lr and wd the way E005's code did for batch 1024, linearly scaled to batch 2000. The frozen group-1 param group keeps its annealed schedule. Batch, epochs, resolution phases, freeze, Lookahead, LS and the SGD groups stay unchanged. Recapture every graph in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: ideate: 3 of 5 members forecast clear harm (median −0.35 pp held-out). At best it saves about 3% (Muon NS overhead), and the tip's discounted population margin (about 0.754 after E038's winner's curse) can't absorb the likely loss. Resolving a loss of 0.15 pp or less would also take more than one 10-seed run. Better candidates (early resolution, staggered freeze, freeze dose) target 2–3% at about zero cost. It can come back if the stem and resolution levers run out.

expected: Time falls about 0.13–0.15 s (23 steps × about 20.4 → 14.4 ms), to about 5.17–5.20 s (−2.5%). E026 and E033 show the first 30% at 20 px is free, so the held-out mean moves between −0.15 and +0.05 pp (median about −0.03). A loss of 0.1 pp or less supports H2.3.6 and puts the early-phase rate above 1.5 s/pp. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means the 20→28 px jump is now too large, and the 24 px bridge carries accuracy.
description: Exploit: finish the early-resolution dial. The tip is E036 (9.25 true epochs, about 231 steps at batch 2000; 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%; whitening bias detached after 20%; group-1 freeze at 75%). Change only the resolution split, from 30/10/30/30 to 40/0/30/30: the 24 px phase (about 23 steps) now runs at 20 px. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions. The LR, Lookahead, whitening-detach and freeze schedules stay unchanged. The 20 px graphs (full and whitening-detached variants) are already captured in build. The 24 px graphs can be dropped from build. error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2, and discount held-out by about 0.1 pp for the winner's curse (E038). Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.

expected: Time falls about 0.17 s (12 × about 14.4 ms), about −3.3%, to about 5.0–5.15 s depending on the base. A uniform trim of the same time costs about 0.11–0.13 pp on the epoch dial. Prediction: held-out falls 0–0.1 pp (median −0.05), which beats the dial at more than 2 s/pp and supports H4.2.5. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means low-res steps count as much as late ones, so uniform trims are the right dial.
description: Exploit: non-uniform trim. Run it on the I-40/0/30/30 successor if kept, otherwise on the E036 tip. Remove only 12 steps from the 20 px phase (231 → 219 total steps). The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening-bias detach stays at the same absolute step (about 46). The group-1 freeze still covers the same last ~58 steps. The LR triangle and the Lookahead ramp are stretched to the new total as fractions, as in E023/E027. No new shapes, so no recapture is needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Run held-out seeds 3–12 in the same session. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.

expected: About 34 extra steps (60–75%, mostly at 28 px) skip the 31×31 backward, at about 3–5 ms each. Time falls 0.10–0.17 s (2–3%), to about 5.15–5.2 s. Held-out moves between −0.25 and 0 pp. A loss of 0.1 pp or less means E037's −0.56 pp came from freezing the deeper group-1 convs, not the full-resolution conv; that supports staggering, and the next step tests conv1 at 50%. A loss of 0.25 pp or more means the first conv itself must adapt through the 28→32 px switch.
description: Explore/exploit: staggered FreezeOut, which separates where E037's cliff came from. First read group 1's structure in the code. If, as in airbench, the pool follows group 1's first conv, that conv (24→128 on 31×31 maps) and the pool are the only full-resolution work left once the whitening is detached. On the E036 tip, put only group 1's first conv in its own Muon param group. Its LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then is annealed to 0 by 60% of steps. From 60% on, detach that conv's output (before the pool), so there is no conv1 wgrad and no pool/BN backward on the 31×31 maps. The rest of group 1 keeps E036's annealed freeze at 75%. Capture the conv1-detached variants at 28 px and 32 px in build, with error_on_recompile on. Lookahead still averages every param. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. If the code shows the pool is not right after conv1, freeze whichever layers run at 31×31 instead, and record which ones.

expected: About 12 more truncated 32 px steps at about 9.5 ms each: time falls about 0.11 s (−2%), to about 5.2 s. Held-out moves between −0.3 and 0 pp. If it falls 0.1 pp or less, the stem needs no 32 px adaptation, the freeze dose was linear-safe down to 70%, and 75% was conservative. If it falls 0.25 pp or more (near E037's per-step rate), the stem must see 32 px before freezing. Then the next test moves the 32 px switch earlier together with the freeze.
description: Freeze-dose test of W5's crux: is E037's cliff caused by freezing before the 28→32 px switch? On the E036 tip, move only the group-1 freeze from 75% to 70% of steps, which is exactly the start of the 32 px phase. The group-1 LR is annealed to 0 by 70% instead of 75%. The truncated 32 px step variant already exists, so no new shapes are needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Steps, resolution phases, LR, Lookahead and the whitening detach are unchanged. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep if held-out ≥ 0.7545 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753.
note: H2.6.4 refuted

expected: Time rises 0.03–0.05 s (about +0.8%; 3 forward passes at about 12 ms each). Held-out moves between −0.1 and +0.25 pp, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp pays for about 0.35 epoch (about 0.24 s), so the booster is net positive. A change within ±0.1 pp means Lookahead's frequent resets already keep the BN stats consistent with the averaged weights. That would close H1.3.6 and, with it, the time-neutral booster search (W3's crux).
description: Time-neutral booster to fund the next trim, re-scoped from the vetoed I015. Two things are different now: the tip has frozen group-1 BN in train mode, and Lookahead lerps BN buffers that were built with momentum 0.6 from different fast weights. On the E036 tip, at the end of train, after the final Lookahead copy: reset every BN layer's running stats and set momentum=None (cumulative average). Then run a no-grad, train-mode forward at 32 px over 3 batches of 2000 training images with the usual crop and flip. Restore BN momentum afterwards. Capture this forward-only train-mode graph in build on synthetic channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Eval stays a plain forward pass. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if held-out gains at least 0.15 pp.
note: ideate: Replaced by the paired BN-recalibration idea (H1.3.6). Evaluating before and after recalibration in the same process removes trajectory and rebuild noise, so the ~0.05 pp effect the committee forecasts becomes measurable. The old design (unpaired seeds 3–12, gate ≥0.15 pp) could not separate it.

expected: If 16 px scales with pixels, about 9 ms per step vs 14.4 ms at 20 px; with the off-grid discount (E024), about 12 ms. Time falls 0.08–0.18 s (1.5–3.5%). Held-out moves −0.3 to 0 pp, median −0.1. A loss of 0.1 pp or less extends the 'early resolution is free' finding below 20 px (rate above 1.5 s/pp). A loss of 0.2 pp or more marks 20 px as the floor for 100 classes.
description: Explore: an even coarser start. On the E036 tip (or the 40/0/30/30 successor if kept), run only the first 15% of steps (about 35) at 16 px instead of 20 px. Map sizes become 15/7/3/1, and the global max-pool head handles 1×1. All other phases, step counts, and the LR, Lookahead, detach and freeze schedules are unchanged. Capture the 16 px graphs in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
note: ideate: The committee agrees (0 improve votes, ~−0.07 s, −0.1 to −0.2 pp expected). E040/E041 show early steps and phase jumps are not free, and saving ~0.07 s for ≥0.1 pp (~0.7 s/pp) is far worse than the epoch dial. Likely dominated.

expected: Trial-0 prepare falls from about 0.15 to about 0.07–0.09 s, so the 3-trial mean time falls about 0.02–0.03 s (−0.4–0.5%). Per-seed accuracy is bit-identical to the base build. If the remainder only appears under the harness process and is not reproducible, record that and close H3.2.
description: Math-identical systems cleanup of trial 0's remaining prepare overhead: about 0.07 s, i.e. 0.148 vs 0.06–0.08 s (E035). In build, make one pageable host-to-device copy of a synthetic CPU uint8 tensor with exactly the training set's shape and dtype. Allocate and free GPU buffers of the sizes prepare uses, so the caching allocator and copy path are warm, and touch the same normalization and whitening ops on that synthetic data. Use no real data. Then add per-op CUDA-event timing to prepare in an offline copy to confirm where the remainder goes before committing. Check with torch.equal that the train tensor and whitening weights are unchanged, so per-seed accuracies stay bit-identical. Record per-trial prepare time.
note: H3 retired

expected: Time rises 0.02–0.05 s (+0.4–1%, to about 5.33–5.36 s). The paired gain per seed should fall between −0.05 and +0.2 pp, median about +0.05. Keep if the mean paired gain is at least +0.05 pp (break-even against the ~1.5 s/pp dial for ≤0.05 s) and positive in at least 13 of 20 seeds. A gain of ≥0.15 pp supports H1.3.6 and pays for about 0.35 epoch of trimming. A gain of ≤0 refutes it: Lookahead's resets every 5 steps already keep the BN stats consistent, which closes the search for a booster that leaves the trajectory unchanged (W3/W6 crux).
description: Exploit: a booster that leaves the training trajectory unchanged. It replaces I064 with a paired design that has no trajectory noise. On the E036 tip, at the end of train() and after the final Lookahead copy (which lerps BN running_mean/var from different fast weights and never recomputes them): reset every BN layer's running stats, set momentum=None (cumulative average), run a no-grad train-mode forward at 32 px over K batches of 2000 training images with the usual crop and flip, then restore momentum. Capture this forward-only graph in build on synthetic channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Eval stays a plain forward pass. Judge it with an offline instrumented copy on unselected seeds 13–32. In each trial, evaluate the averaged model once before recalibration and once after, so the two numbers share the exact same trained weights and the difference has no trajectory or rebuild noise. Do the same for K=1 and K=3. Commit the better K, then run ar.py to get time and the seeds 0–2 check. The submission evaluates only once.

expected: Time rises 0.05–0.12 s (+1–2.5%), from about 69 extra 20 px steps at roughly 1–1.5 ms of overhead each plus lower kernel efficiency at batch 1000. The held-out 20-seed mean should move between 0 and +0.3 pp, median about +0.1. A gain of ≥0.15 pp supports H5.2 and is a better booster than epochs (≥1.5 pp per s). It would also fund E040/E041-style early trims. A change of ≤+0.05 pp refutes the step-count reading: E041's cost then came from compressing the LR schedule, and early batch size is a dead lever (which also settles H5.1.3/H5.2.1 without running them).
description: Explore/booster, the step-count crux (W3, W5). E041 found that removing early 20 px steps cost as much as a uniform trim. That suggests early accuracy is carried by optimizer steps, not by pixels. On the E036 tip, use batch 1000 instead of 2000 only during the 20 px phase (the first 30% of data passes, so about 69 steps become about 138). Same data and same pixels; only the step count and per-step overhead change. Key the LR triangle, the whitening-bias detach (20%) and the resolution switch to data progress (samples seen), so they land at the same data point. In this phase, scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×0.5) and keep the Muon lr per step unchanged. Lookahead stays every 5 steps; alpha is near 0 this early. From 24 px on, batch 2000 is unchanged, so the 24/28/32 phases, freeze and Lookahead tail are identical. Capture batch-1000 graphs at 20 px, both the full and whitening-detached variants, in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds (reuse E038's 13–22 and run E036 once on 23–32; the C/D/selection ideas share this baseline), plus seeds 0–2.
note: committee veto AUDIT: run it to measure the veto

expected: Time rises 0.15–0.30 s (+3–6%, to about 5.5–5.6 s), from 77 extra steps of fixed overhead plus lower tile efficiency. The held-out mean should move between −0.1 and +0.4 pp, median about +0.15. The change is net positive if the gain is at least Δtime/1.5 s/pp (≈0.15 pp for +0.22 s); a trim can then cash it in. A gain under 0.1 pp means batch 2000 is at or below the useful critical batch, which closes H5.1 toward smaller batches.
description: Explore, the batch-size crux named by W2, W5 and W6. On the E036 tip at the same true epoch count (9.25), lower the batch from 2000 to 1500 everywhere: 33 steps per epoch with the ragged batch dropped, so about 308 steps instead of 231. Scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×0.75). Muon lr per step and momentum 0.6 stay unchanged. The resolution phases, LR triangle, Lookahead ramp (still every 5 steps), whitening detach (20%) and group-1 freeze (75%) stay as fractions of the new step count. Recapture every resolution and variant at batch 1500 in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2. Hiverge's record uses 1536 under Muon. I026 (1250, older base) was vetoed, but E041 has since shown that steps carry accuracy.
note: committee veto: 4/4 members forecast clear harm, none an improvement

expected: Time falls 0.12–0.20 s (−2.5 to −4%, to about 5.12–5.2 s), since group-2 wgrad and dgrad are about 30% of a frozen 32 px step. The held-out mean should move between −0.3 and 0 pp, median about −0.1. Supports H2.6.8 if the loss is ≤0.1 pp, a rate of ≥1.5 s/pp that beats the epoch dial. It can then be stacked with a booster (BN recalibration or early small batch) to get back over the bar. A loss of ≥0.2 pp means the deep features still move usefully during the averaging window, and the cascade stops at group 1.
description: Exploit, staggered FreezeOut cascade. This is the only remaining backward-truncation lever that targets the largest block, group 2 (~51% of conv MACs). On the E036 tip, put the group-2 conv filters (Muon) and group-2 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR follows the global schedule until 75%, then decays linearly to 0 by 90% of steps; E028's annealed freeze is what kept group 1 neutral. For the last 10% of steps (about 23 steps, 32 px, group 1 already frozen), detach group 2's output before group 3 and use a new compiled 32 px step with no group-1/2 backward and no update for those params. Group-2 BN stays in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture the new variant in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2.

expected: Time and accuracy are unchanged. Predictions: GPU idle plus non-step work under 5% of train time; non-GEMM kernels at least 30% of a 32 px full step (H6.3.1); conv1 below half of group-2 TFLOP/s with about 50% probability (H6.4.1); 24 px layer-weighted throughput within 20% of 32 px (H6.1.1 likely refuted). Decision rules: if conv1 is under half of group-2 efficiency and at least 10% of step time, raise the Cin-padding idea (H6.4.2) to priority 4. If idle plus augmentation is over 5%, queue a systems fix. Otherwise close H6's systems branch, leaving step count and backward truncation as the only levers.
description: Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It replaces I058 and adds the overhead accounting from W5's crux. Offline, on the E036 tip with synthetic channels_last data at batch 2000: (1) torch.profiler traces of the compiled 32 px full step, the whitening-detached step, the frozen step and the 20/24 px steps. Record GPU time by kernel class (conv fwd/dgrad/wgrad, BN, GELU, pool, elementwise, Muon NS, Lookahead) and by layer, plus achieved TFLOP/s per conv. Explicitly compare group-1 conv1 (Cin=24, 31×31) against the group-2 convs. (2) One trace of a whole timed train() for seed 13 on real data. Record GPU idle fraction, per-epoch augmentation/interpolate/permute time, and time outside the step graphs. Write the table to the notebook, and label each kept lever as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound (H4.3). Do not edit submissions/arena/.

expected: Time falls 0.2–0.28 s (−4 to −5%, to about 5.05–5.1 s). A uniform cut of the same steps costs about 0.15–0.18 pp on the dial. The held-out mean should move between −0.25 and 0 pp, median about −0.12. A loss of ≤0.1 pp supports H2.7.1 (selection beats a uniform trim) and makes it stackable with a booster. A loss of ≥0.18 pp means selection is no better than the dial, which closes H2.7.
description: Exploit, a milder dose of the E031 near-miss. E031's top-90% selection cost −0.27 pp for −0.63 s (~2.3 s/pp, nominally better than the dial but within noise). On the E036 tip, return per-sample losses from the compiled step (reduction='none', then mean for backward) and scatter them into a GPU buffer indexed by sample id, created and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 on, each epoch's shuffle uses only the 95% of samples with the highest loss in the previous pass (topk on the GPU), with batch 2000 and the ragged batch dropped. Total steps fall from about 231 to about 220. The resolution phases, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach and freeze stay as fractions of the new step count. Warm up the modified step variants in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2.

expected: Time changes by −2% to +1%. Cin=24 is already a multiple of 8, so the alignment gain may not cover conv1's +33% FLOPs in fwd/wgrad. Accuracy should stay within rebuild noise (3-seed mean within 0.1 pp; per-seed shifts up to ~0.3 pp from kernel reselection). A time cut of ≥2% supports H6.4.2 and comes at no accuracy cost, which matters at zero margin. Under 1% refutes it, and the misaligned channel count is not the stem cost.
description: Exploit, systems only, with identical math. On the E036 tip, widen the frozen whitening conv's output from 24 to 32 channels with 8 zero filters and a zero, detached bias. Widen group-1 conv1's input to 32 channels, with zero weights on the 8 new input channels. Initialize at the original shape first, then pad, so RNG consumption is unchanged. Under Muon, those columns stay exactly zero: their gradient is zero, NS left-multiplication keeps zero columns zero, and norms and wd are unaffected. GELU(0)=0 keeps the padded activations zero. Eval uses the padded net. Before launching, check offline that the padded and unpadded forward outputs match (allclose in fp16) on the same weights, and that the padded weights stay exactly 0 after 20 training steps. Recapture every graph in build, with error_on_recompile on. Best run after the profiling diagnostic; raise priority if it shows conv1 is inefficient.
note: ideate: E047 settled this: conv1 (Cin=24) runs at about 0.45x group-2 efficiency but costs only 6–9% of a 32 px step, with dgrad already skipped after the whitening detach. That is below H6.4.1's 10% bar. Padding to Cin=32 adds 33% of conv1's MACs, and all four committee members forecast no improvement (0/4 improve votes).

expected: Time +0.12 to +0.17 s (to about 5.43–5.48 s, +2.5–3%), because part of the added work lands in cheap frozen 32 px steps. The 20-seed mean rises 0.06–0.15 pp over same-build E036 (median +0.10, to about 0.7545). That puts the post-freeze dial at about 1.0–2 s/pp. A gain under 0.05 pp means the dial has flattened near the tip, so margin must come from structure (H1.7) instead.
description: Exploit: buy margin, as the H4 gate requires before any further time cut. On the E036 tip (231 steps at batch 2000), change only the step count to 9.5 true epochs (237 steps), adding 0.25 epoch. Keep the 20/24/28/32 px phases (30/10/30/30), the LR triangle, the Lookahead ramp, the whitening-bias detach (20%) and the group-1 freeze (75%) as fractions of the new total, as in E023/E027/E034. No new shapes, so no recapture is needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Run it in ONE build session: (a) E036 unchanged on seeds 13–32, a fresh same-build baseline that I075 and later ideas reuse; (b) this recipe on seeds 13–32; (c) ar.py on seeds 0–2. Keep if the 20-seed mean is ≥0.7545 and seeds 0–2 are ≥0.753 in this build. Also record the measured s/pp so the post-freeze dial gets re-priced for every later booster and cut. Do not re-roll RNG streams.
note: committee veto: 3/4 members forecast clear harm, none an improvement

expected: Time about 5.18–5.24 s (−1.5 to −2.5% vs E036): E046's −0.23 s plus the top-up's +0.13 s. 20-seed mean −0.15 to +0.08 pp vs same-build E036 (median −0.03).
description: Exploit, the decisive test of the E046 crux (W2/W3/W5/W6). On the E036 tip, apply E046's group-2 freeze exactly as committed in 8a2452a. Group-2 filters and BN params get their own groups, with LR annealed from 75% to 0 at 90% of steps. For the last 10% of steps, group 2's output is detached before group 3, using the truncated 32 px variant. Group-2 BN stays in train mode and Lookahead averages every param. On top of that, add 0.25 true epoch (231 → 237 steps, all schedules kept as fractions). Capture the variants in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge in the same build session as I074, against the same-build E036 baseline and the I074 arm on seeds 13–32, plus seeds 0–2. Decision: if time is at least 2% below E036 and the 20-seed mean is within 0.03 pp of E036 or above it, the cascade-plus-top-up dominates E036 and becomes the base for further margin buying. If it trails the I074 arm by more than 0.15 pp, the group-2 freeze is no better than the dial and the cascade closes.

expected: Time −0.03 to −0.08 s (−0.5 to −1.5%, to about 5.24–5.29 s). Accuracy unchanged per seed. If the copies turn out to be the cudagraph's own unavoidable parameter or static-input traffic (saving <0.5%), close the non-step systems branch for good.
description: Exploit, systems only, with identical math. E047's whole-trial trace found about 135 ms (2.5%) of non-step GPU work: memcpy/copies 68 ms, interpolate 29 ms, augmentation gathers 20 ms, permutation indexing 12 ms. First, in an offline copy, attribute the 68 ms of copies with torch.profiler stack traces. Likely sources are cudagraph-tree copy-in of the augmented batch into static inputs, channels_last .contiguous() after interpolate, and the dataset index_select. Then remove them without changing any number. Have the crop/flip/interpolate path write directly into the step graph's static input buffer, or move augmentation inside the compiled step. Do the per-epoch permutation gather once per epoch as one batched gather instead of per-batch indexing. Drop redundant layout conversions. Before launching, check offline with torch.equal that every batch tensor equals the current one for seed 13. Capture in build, with error_on_recompile on. Keep on time alone if seeds 0–2 accuracies are bit-identical to the same-build baseline, or within rebuild noise if kernels were re-selected.
note: Settled by offline attribution on the E036/E049 code path (real data, seed 13 trial, profiler): copies = 12139 tiny DtoD memcpys (32.7 ms, ~51/step at ~2.7 us: Muon mutated-input write-backs + Lookahead foreach copies), direct_copy kernels 14 ms (fp16 casts/contiguous), memsets 20 ms (grad zeroing/allocator), pageable HtoD 10.7 ms (dataset transfer in prepare); GPU idle 3.0%. Removable share is <~0.5% of the trial and largely overlapped with compute -> below I076's own closing threshold; non-step systems branch closed.

expected: Time +0.12 to +0.20 s (+2.5–4%). 20-seed mean −0.05 to +0.30 pp (median +0.10). A gain of ≥0.15 pp at ≤+3% supports H1.7 (late capacity is the CIFAR-100 bottleneck) and beats the dial. A gain of ≤0.05 pp refutes the late-capacity reading and leaves epochs as the only booster.
description: Explore, the structural sample-efficiency lever H1 calls for. It is cheaper than H1.7.1's widening, which would add about 7% time (E010's 576→512 saved 4.8%). On the E036 tip, add a fourth 3×3 conv (512→512, BN, GELU) to group 3's residual branch after conv3 and before the residual add. It runs on 3×3 maps at 32 px (2–3 px at lower resolutions), where E047 measured the convs at about 1.1 ms fwd+bwd per 32 px step. Give it Dirac init like the others so it starts near identity. Initialize it after the existing layers so their init RNG draws are unchanged. It joins the Muon group, with the same wd and LR schedule, and is averaged by Lookahead. Recapture every resolution and variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against the same-build E036 baseline (I074's session if available), plus seeds 0–2. Booster rule: worth keeping if the gain is ≥ Δtime / (I074's measured s/pp).
note: committee veto: 4/4 members forecast clear harm, none an improvement

expected: Time −0.5 to −3% (median −1.2%). 20-seed mean −0.4 to 0 pp (median −0.15), since GELU usually beats ReLU in short runs. Supports H6.5.1 only if time falls ≥3% with ≤0.15 pp loss. A saving under 1% shows the fused kernels are bytes-bound and closes the activation branch of H6.5.
description: Explore, the memory-bound share (27% of the 32 px step, E043). On the E036 tip, replace GELU with ReLU in all conv groups. If any activation sits before group 1 or in the head, leave it unchanged. Nothing else changes. Inspect Inductor's saved tensors offline first: record whether ReLU's backward saves a bool mask or the fp16 output, since that sets the bytes saved. Recapture every resolution and variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against the same-build E036 baseline, plus seeds 0–2. This settles whether the fused BN/activation kernels are bytes-bound (activation type irrelevant) or compute-sensitive (GELU's erf costs time).
note: ideate: Replaced by a gated version. All four members forecast a ~2% saving and a −0.15 pp loss (0 improve votes), which is a worse rate than the epoch dial. The only open question is whether the saving reaches 3%, and an offline step-time benchmark answers that before any 20-seed run is spent.

expected: (1) Bit-identical, about 85% likely. (2) Bit-identical across rebuilds, about 70% likely, at +0.3 to +1.0% time (E015's cudagraph gain was −0.9%). (3) Bit-identical with about 0% time change, if the cache is allowed. Accuracy is unchanged in distribution, but the 3-seed mean lands at one fixed value, about 0.750–0.754. If (1) fails, nondeterministic kernels cause the spread, pinning cannot help, and every comparison must stay at 20 seeds per arm. Time objective: change between −0.2% and +1%, so this is not expected to produce a new best by itself.
description: Explore diagnostic plus systems change, with identical math. Recent keep and discard decisions are noise-limited: E042, E045, E046 and E048 all landed between their thresholds, and the tip's seeds 0–2 mean has read 0.7532 / 0.7525 / 0.7497 / 0.7544 across four builds of the same commit. Before any further sub-0.15 pp comparison, find out whether that build-to-build spread can be removed. Run offline on the E036 tip (commit 60645dd) through the harness code path, seeds 0–2. (1) Build once, then run seeds 0–2 twice in the same process. Record whether per-seed accuracies are bit-identical, which tests for within-build nondeterminism such as cuDNN wgrad atomics. (2) Build twice in fresh processes with private inductor cache dirs, using mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' for every step variant.
