Compare per-seed accuracies across the two builds and record mean time against the E036 build. (3) Keep max-autotune with cudagraphs, but pin kernel choice by persisting the inductor/autotune cache under submissions/arena/. Populate it from a synthetic-data build only, never real data. Do two fresh-process builds that read the pinned cache and compare per-seed accuracies. First check RULES.md and the submission contract to confirm that a shipped compile cache is allowed. If it is not, report arm (3) as diagnostic only. Commit only if arm (2) or arm (3) is bit-identical across rebuilds at ≤0.5% time cost versus E036. In that case it becomes the deterministic baseline, and every later idea compares seeds 0–2 and 13–32 against it exactly.

expected: conv1 FLOPs fall about 4×, and the 128×31×31 write/read and pool backward disappear. Expect about −3 to −5 ms per unfrozen 32 px step and −1.5 to −2.5 ms per frozen step, proportionally less at low resolution. Total time −5 to −9% (about 4.85–5.05 s). 20-seed mean −0.6 to 0 pp, median −0.25: learned strided downsampling loses max-pool's local translation invariance. It beats the epoch dial (~1.5 s/pp) if the loss is ≤0.25 pp for ≥0.35 s. That would make it the base for an epoch top-up that nets a feasible time below E036. A loss ≥0.4 pp means the stem needs full-resolution conv features and closes the stem-structure branch of H2.5.
description: Explore/exploit: remove the last full-resolution tensor from the stem. E047 measured g1.conv1 (24→128 at 31×31) at about 0.45× group-2 efficiency, and the 128-channel 31×31 activation feeding the max-pool is the largest memory-bound tensor in the net. E043/E028 showed the stem's 31×31 work costs far more than its FLOP share. On the E036 tip, replace group 1's 'conv1 (3×3, pad 1) → 2×2 max-pool' with a single 3×3 conv with stride 2 and padding 0 (31→15, the same 15×15 output as now, so groups 2/3 and their map sizes 15/7/3 are unchanged at 32 px). At 28/24/20 px it gives 13/11/9, which also matches the current pool outputs; verify this for each resolution in code. Keep the same channel counts, BN-GELU after it, init scheme and RNG draw order (same weight shape). The whitening detach (20%) and group-1 freeze (75%) stay unchanged. Recapture every resolution and variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E036 baseline, plus seeds 0–2. Record the per-step time at 32 px (full and frozen) for the H6 accounting.

expected: Time −2 to −3.5% vs the base (about 0.10–0.18 s; on I075's base that is about 5.05–5.1 s, below E036's 5.31). 20-seed mean −0.15 to +0.05 pp vs the base, median −0.05. Selection's measured rate (E048 ~1.85 s/pp) should slightly beat the top-up. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 and the 20-seed mean ≥0.7545 (or within 0.03 pp of the same-build E036). A loss ≥0.12 pp vs the base means selection is no better than the dial once paid for, which closes H2.7.
description: Exploit, combining two near-misses. Conditional: run only after I075 reports. Base: I075's recipe (group-2 freeze plus a +0.25 epoch top-up) if its 20-seed mean is within 0.03 pp of same-build E036 or above it; otherwise E036. Add E048's loss-based selection exactly as committed in 4ffd290: per-sample losses from the compiled step are scattered into a GPU buffer reset in prepare, and from epoch 2 on each epoch shuffles only the 95% highest-loss samples, with the ragged batch dropped. Also add a further +0.25 true epoch, so the net step count falls by only about 5 steps rather than E048's 11. Resolution, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach and freeze points all stay as fractions of the new step count. Capture the modified variants in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against the base and E036 in the same build session, plus seeds 0–2. This answers W3's crux in its stackable form: does selection beat the dial once the dial's top-up pays for it?

expected: Time about −0.12 to −0.15 s more (13 steps × about 10 ms saved per E046), about −2.5% vs I075's recipe, to about 4.95–5.05 s. 20-seed mean −0.25 to 0 pp vs I075's recipe, median −0.08. Supports a longer cascade if the loss is ≤0.08 pp (rate ≥1.5 s/pp). A loss ≥0.15 pp means group 2 must keep learning through the first part of the 32 px averaging window, which caps the cascade at 10%.
description: Exploit, freeze-dose extension of the cascade (W6's crux). Conditional: run only if I075 keeps, i.e. the group-2 freeze plus top-up is within 0.03 pp of same-build E036 at ≥2% less time. On I075's recipe, move the group-2 freeze start from 90% to 85% of steps, with the group-2 LR annealed from 70% (the 32 px switch) to 0 by 85%. The frozen-group-2 32 px variant then covers the last 15% (about 36 steps instead of 23). Nothing else changes, including the step count, group-1 freeze at 75%, whitening detach, Lookahead and resolution. The variant already exists, so no new shapes are needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against I075's recipe and E036 in the same build session, plus seeds 0–2.
note: Identical to I083, run as E053 on the E049 tip: g2 freeze 85% (anneal from 70%) -> 5.07 s but seeds 13-32 -0.24 pp vs E049. Refuted; g2 freeze stays at 90%.

expected: Time −0.10 to −0.15 s (about −2.5%, to about 5.05–5.10 s). 20-seed mean −0.25 to 0 pp vs same-build E049 (median −0.08). A loss of ≤0.08 pp supports extending the cascade (rate ≥1.5 s/pp) and feeds the stacking idea. A loss of ≥0.15 pp caps the cascade at 10%.
description: Keep I082 as queued: the group-2 freeze dose test. Base: the E049 tip (237 steps; group-2 LR annealed 75%→0 at 90%; last 10% group-2-frozen). Move the group-2 freeze start from 90% to 85% of steps, with the group-2 LR annealed from 70% (the 32 px switch) to 0 by 85%. The frozen-group-2 32 px variant then covers about 36 steps instead of 24. Nothing else changes: step count, group-1 freeze at 75%, whitening detach at 20%, Lookahead and resolution all stay. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E049 baseline, plus seeds 0–2. This settles the W2/W3/W5 crux on whether group 2 has a cliff like E037's.

expected: About 35 steps save ~5.5–6 ms each, so time falls 0.15–0.22 s (−3 to −4%, to about 4.98–5.05 s). 20-seed mean −0.3 to +0.05 pp (median −0.10). Keep if the loss is ≤0.10 pp and seeds 0–2 ≥0.753 (rate ≥1.5 s/pp, better than the dial). A loss of ≥0.2 pp means stem learning in the 28 px phase is per-step-limited, which closes backward truncation before 75%.
description: Explore, proposing a new H2.6 child: the stem needs a steady adaptation signal, not a gradient on every step. Intermittent stem backward in the 28 px phase, which is the most expensive phase (about 71 steps × ~26 ms ≈ 1.8 s). On the E049 tip, on every second step of the 28 px phase (40–70% of steps), use the group-1-detached 28 px step variant. That variant has no group-1 wgrad/dgrad and no BN/GELU backward on the stem maps, and group-1 params get no Muon/SGD update and no momentum-buffer change on those steps. The variant already existed in E037's commit 6293350. On the other steps, run the usual whitening-detached full step with the group-1 LR as scheduled. Do not rescale the LR: single factor. Group 1 still trains on every step at 20/24 px and from 70% to 75% at 32 px, so it still adapts through the 28→32 switch, which E037/E042 say it needs. Lookahead averages every param. Capture the variant in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E049 baseline, plus seeds 0–2.

expected: About 9–10 more frozen steps at ~7.7 ms each: time −0.05 to −0.08 s (~−1.3%, to about 5.13 s). Linear extrapolation from E037 (−0.56 pp for 15% earlier) predicts about −0.15 pp. The cliff reading (H2.6.7) predicts ≤0.05 pp. Median forecast −0.07 pp. A loss of ≤0.05 pp supports H2.6.7 and opens 'move the 32 px switch earlier together with the freeze'. A loss of ≥0.12 pp supports a linear dose and closes the group-1 freeze point at 75%.
description: Decisive test of E037's mechanism: a 32 px adaptation cliff, or a linear freeze dose? On the E049 tip, move only the group-1 freeze start from 75% to 71% of steps, just after the 28→32 px switch at 70% (about step 168 of 237). Group 1 then sees about 2 steps at 32 px before its LR reaches 0. Anneal the group-1 LR from its peak to 0 by 71% instead of 75%. The group-2 freeze, whitening detach, step count, resolution, LR and Lookahead are unchanged. The truncated 32 px variant exists, so there are no new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E049 baseline, plus seeds 0–2. The result also sets the prior for the intermittent-stem idea.

expected: Most likely (consensus ~2%) step 1 projects a 1–2.5% saving and the branch closes at near-zero cost. If ≥3%: time −3 to −4% (about −0.16 s) and 20-seed mean −0.35 to 0 pp (median −0.15). Keep only if the loss is ≤0.1 pp, which the rate requires.
description: Sharpened replacement for I078, gated on the committee's shared crux (do ReLU's saved bytes reach 3%?). Step 1 is offline, with no repo change. On the E049 tip code with synthetic channels_last batch-2000 data, compile the 32 px whitening-detached, group-1-frozen and group-1+2-frozen steps and the 28 px step twice: GELU vs ReLU in all conv groups. Measure GPU kernel time per step (torch.profiler, 20 steps each), and record whether Inductor's ReLU backward saves a bool mask or the fp16 output. Weight the per-step savings by the tip's step counts per phase. Step 2 runs only if the projected saving is ≥3% of train time: commit the ReLU swap, recapture every variant in build with error_on_recompile on, and judge on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E049 baseline plus seeds 0–2. If the projected saving is under 3%, close H6.5's activation branch with no run.

expected: With both cuts: time about 4.95–5.05 s (−0.30 s from the cuts, +0.12 s for the top-up; −3 to −5% vs E049). 20-seed mean −0.1 to +0.1 pp vs E049 (median 0), which moves toward the 0.7545 gate. With one cut: time −1 to −2% at about equal accuracy.
description: Conditional stacking and margin idea: run after I082 and the intermittent-stem idea report. Take every per-step cut that passed its own same-build test (I082's 85% group-2 freeze with a loss of ≤0.08 pp; intermittent 28 px stem backward with a loss of ≤0.10 pp; and, if positive, the selection arm of I081). Stack them on the E049 tip and add +0.25 true epoch (237 → about 243 steps). Keep all freeze, detach, resolution, LR and Lookahead points as step fractions. Capture every variant in build with error_on_recompile on. Judge in one build session: same-build E049 on seeds 13–32, this recipe on seeds 13–32, and ar.py on seeds 0–2. Keep if time is ≥1.5% below E049, the 20-seed mean is ≥ E049's same-build mean (target ≥0.7545, the H4 gate), and seeds 0–2 ≥0.753. Record the measured s/pp of the post-cascade dial. If neither cut passed, drop this idea.
note: Its own rule: drop if neither cut passed. 85% g2 freeze (E053: -0.24 pp), intermittent 28 px stem backward (E054: -0.48 pp) and selection (E052: -0.21 pp) all failed their same-tip tests on seeds 13-32.

expected: Time unchanged (~5.20 s; builds within ~1% of each other). The 20-seed means of the three builds spread 0.03–0.20 pp (median range ~0.08), and per-seed build differences correlate positively, so σ_build ≈ 0.04–0.1 pp. E049's fresh mean is 0.7520–0.7545 (median ~0.7532), about 0.05 pp below its 13–32 reading. H4.4.3 is supported if the drop is ≥0.1 pp and refuted if within 0.05 pp. H4.5.1 is refuted if the build means differ by <0.04 pp.
description: Diagnostic with no recipe change. It feeds the frozen keep gate (H4.6) and also settles H4.4.3. Build the E049 tip (commit 3df6233) three times, each in a fresh process with its own private TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR. Run each build through the harness code path on fresh seeds 33–52 (benchmark.run --seed 33 --n 20) and on seeds 0–2. Record: per-seed accuracies for every build; the three 20-seed means; the per-seed differences between builds and their correlation across seeds; and mean time per build. Derive the rebuild SD σ_build of a 20-seed mean as the SD of the three means, after subtracting the expected per-seed-noise part (SD_seed/√20 × √2 for a difference). Also report E049's pooled fresh mean against its 0.7539 on reused seeds 13–32 (winner's curse, H4.4.3). Do not edit submissions/arena/. From now on, seeds 33–52 are the decision set and seeds 53–72 are reserved for one final confirmation per candidate.

expected: E052 fresh mean 0.7505–0.7535 (median ~0.7520). E053 0.7500–0.7535 (median ~0.7518). Deficit vs E049 on the same fresh seeds 0.05–0.25 pp (median ~0.13), smaller than on reused seeds 13–32 (−0.21/−0.24). With σ_tot ≈ 0.10–0.14 pp the gate threshold is ≈0.7517–0.7523, so E052 passes with ~45% probability. If it passes and is confirmed, the tip moves to ~4.99 s (−4%). If neither passes, the gate stays near 0.752 and is recorded as the frozen rule.
description: Exploit plus a gate test. It may re-keep a faster recipe that has already been measured. Before reading any number, freeze the keep gate. Let μ̂ be a candidate's 20-seed mean on seeds 33–52. Let σ_tot = sqrt(SE20² + SD_seed²/40 + σ_build² + 0.05²), with σ_build taken from the H4.5.1 idea and 0.05 pp as the PCIe judge-drift term. Gate: μ̂ − 1.64·σ_tot ≥ 0.7500 (P(official ≥0.75) ≥ 0.95), and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 on the candidate's single committed build, with no rebuilding to chase a draw. Then build E052 (ce17ae7, 4.99 s) and E053 (f30d362, 5.07 s) once each in the same session as the H4.5.1 builds, and run each on seeds 33–52 and seeds 0–2. Pick the fastest candidate that passes. Confirm it once on reserved seeds 53–72, where it must pass the gate again, to undo the selection among candidates. Only then re-keep it, using its ar.py result from that one build. No recipe edits: both commits already exist.

expected: Time −0.10 to −0.14 s vs E049 (E046 measured 5.08 s). Fresh 20-seed mean 0.06–0.20 pp below E049 (median −0.12), giving a dial of ~0.6–2 s/pp (median ~1 s/pp). A loss below 0.06 pp means the top-up in E049 bought nothing and E046 dominates E049. A loss above 0.2 pp means the post-freeze dial is steep (<0.6 s/pp), so the remaining cuts are all too expensive.
description: Re-measure the post-freeze epoch dial in the time-favourable direction, with no new code. E049 minus 0.25 true epoch is exactly E046 (commit 8a2452a: same group-2 freeze at 231 steps, all schedules as fractions). In the same session as the H4.5.1 builds, build E046 once and run it on seeds 33–52 and seeds 0–2. Compute dial = Δtime / Δacc against E049's builds on the same seeds, adding σ_build to the SE of the difference. Use the result to re-price every booster and cut, and to resolve the 0.7 vs 1.5 s/pp dispute in H4.2. E046 also enters the frozen gate as a candidate (it was feasible locally at 0.7540 / 5.08 s); if it is the fastest passing candidate, it goes through the 53–72 confirmation under the H4.6.1 idea's rule.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 20-seed mean −0.10 to +0.25 pp vs E049 (median +0.05). A gain of ≥0.12 pp supports H1.8.1 and is worth ~0.1–0.2 s at the measured dial, which can be cashed in by a −0.25 epoch trim (the E046 step count). A change within ±0.05 pp closes H1.8, along with the last scalar-free booster family.
description: Explore, a time-neutral structural booster. Step 0: read RULES.md and the benchmark data loader. Run only if the 50k training set as shipped includes CIFAR-100 coarse labels (for example 'coarse_labels' in the train pickle). If the fine→coarse mapping would have to come from a hard-coded external table, treat it as external data, mark H1.8 blocked, and do not run. If allowed: in timed prepare, read the training coarse labels and build a 100×100 soft-target matrix T on the GPU. Each row gets 0.70 on the true class, 0.15 spread uniformly over all 100 classes, and 0.15 spread over the 4 other fine classes in the same superclass. Train with soft-target cross-entropy against T[y] in place of LS 0.3 (total smoothing mass unchanged). Warm up in build with a synthetic T of the same shape and dtype, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2.
note: Blocked by its own step 0: the harness passes TrainingData(images, labels) with fine labels only (benchmark/api.py, data.py); coarse labels would require reading dataset files outside the API or a hard-coded fine->coarse table, which the idea itself classifies as external data.

expected: If the port trains BN scale: time −0.3 to −1.0% (fewer optimizer and fused-backward reads), and the 20-seed mean within ±0.1 pp (median 0). Keep if per-step timing shows ≥0.5% saved and the candidate passes the frozen gate. A loss of ≥0.15 pp refutes it: BN scale carries capacity in the 100-way short run.
description: Fidelity check, code first. Read the port's BatchNorm setup. If every BN weight (scale) already has requires_grad=False (as in airbench96/Hiverge), close H1.5.10 with no run. If the port trains BN scale: on the E049 tip, set BN weight requires_grad=False at its init value of 1 in every BN layer, and remove those tensors from the SGD group and from Lookahead's averaged set. Keep the init RNG draw order unchanged. Recapture every resolution and step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2, with per-step CUDA-event timing to separate the time effect from build noise.
note: Closed by its own code check: BatchNorm.__init__ sets self.weight.requires_grad = False (BN scale frozen at 1, as in airbench), so there is nothing to change.

expected: Per-step timing shows −0.02 to −0.04 s per trial (−0.3 to −0.7%). Wall time 5.16–5.20 s. 20-seed mean within ±0.08 pp of E049 (median −0.02). Supported if the loss is ≤0.05 pp; then it is a free stackable cut. A loss of ≥0.12 pp means the bias adapts through the 20→24 px switch.
description: Exploit, a near-free truncation. On the E049 tip, move the whitening-bias detach from 20% to 6% of steps (about step 14 of 237, inside the 20 px phase), with the whitening-bias LR annealed to 0 by 6% instead of 20%. The whitening-detached variants already exist at every resolution, so there are no new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Everything else is unchanged. Measure the saving with per-step CUDA-event timing (the expected effect is below the ~1% rebuild time spread) as well as wall time. Judge accuracy on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2. Consult the H7.1.1 curves if they are available first.

expected: No change to the task metrics (time and accuracy are those of E049). Prediction: the whitening bias settles by ~5–10% of steps, and groups 1 and 2 cross the 10% threshold near 72–76% and 88–92%. If the curves place group 1's threshold before 60% (failing to separate E028 from E037), the learning-finished account is refuted as a predictor and freeze points must stay empirical.
description: Explore diagnostic, offline, outside submissions/arena/. Instrument a copy of the E049 tip, run it on real data for seeds 33–35, and every 5 steps log ||ΔW||/||W|| for the whitening bias, group-1 convs, group-1 BN, group-2 convs, group-2 BN, group-3 convs, group-3 BN and the head, plus each group's gradient norm relative to its own peak. Mark the resolution switches, the LR peak, the anneal starts and the freeze points. Check whether the curves order the known outcomes: whitening bias below 10% of its peak rate by ≤10% of steps; group 1 only after ~70% (E028 free, E037/E054/E055 costly); group 2 only after ~88% (E046 marginal, E053 costly). Report the curves in the notebook.
note: ideate: The committee agrees (W3, W5) that under Muon the orthogonalized updates have a fixed norm, so ||ΔW||/||W|| just tracks the imposed LR schedule and cannot separate E028 from E037. It is also an offline diagnostic with no score path. The freeze points it would predict are already mapped empirically (group 1 at 75%, group 2 at 90%, whitening detach being tested in I093), and groups 3 and the head cannot be frozen.

expected: Time about −0.15 s (12 × about 14 ms), to about 5.03–5.07 s (−3%). 40-draw mean −0.20 to 0 pp vs 0.7534 (median −0.08). A loss of ≤0.15 pp beats the dial (≥1 s/pp) and supports H4.2.5. Such a cut is stackable with the selection/top-up ideas. A loss of ≥0.2 pp confirms that early steps cost as much as a uniform trim and closes non-uniform trims.
description: Exploit: re-test a near-miss that was discarded on biased seeds, now priced at the new dial. E041 (remove 12 early 20 px steps) read −0.20 pp on seeds 3–12 right after those seeds selected E036, and that was already about the new 0.77 s/pp dial. On the E049 tip, remove only 12 steps from the 20 px phase (237 → 225). The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening detach stays at the same absolute step, and the group-1 and group-2 freezes cover the same last absolute steps. The LR triangle and Lookahead ramp are stretched to the new total as fractions, as in E041. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (40 draws) against E049's 60 draws, then the frozen gate on the single committed build.

expected: Time −3 to −4.5% (about −0.15 to −0.22 s, to about 5.0 s). 40-draw mean −0.5 to +0.1 pp vs 0.7534 (median −0.2). A loss of ≤0.15 pp means Muon is not buying its cost on CIFAR-100 (it supports PR #3 and refutes H1.2.2's ≥0.3 pp prediction). It would then be a cut stackable with a top-up that nets about −0.1 s. A loss of ≥0.3 pp supports H1.2.2 and keeps Muon.
description: Explore, the largest untested optimizer axis. It is now cheap to judge because the break-even loss is about 0.25 pp at the 0.77 s/pp dial. On the E049 tip, replace Muon on every conv filter group (group 1, group 2 and group 3) with Nesterov SGD. Use momentum 0.85, airbench's value, as in E005's commit ac425fc. Use the E005 conv lr, scaled linearly from batch 1024 to 2000 the way the port's airbench lr normalization already does, and wd ×0.5 as in E016. Each filter group keeps its own LR schedule, including the anneal-to-0 at 75% for group 1 and the 75→90% anneal for group 2. The freeze, detach, resolution, step count, Lookahead, LS and SGD groups are all unchanged. Init RNG draw order is unchanged. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Record per-step CUDA-event time to isolate the Newton–Schulz saving (about 0.8 ms per step × 237 steps, per E043). Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E049's 60 draws. PR #3 (CIFAR-100, airbench96) reports SGD beating Muon at every size. E006's +0.66 pp confounded Muon with the batch change from 1024 to 2000 and an RNG re-draw.

expected: Step 1: tanh-GELU saves 0–1.5% and SiLU saves 1–3% (it needs only one exp). If a run happens: time −1.5 to −3%. Accuracy: tanh-GELU within ±0.05 pp; SiLU −0.3 to +0.05 pp (median −0.1). Keep only if the loss is ≤ saving / 0.77 s/pp (e.g. ≤0.13 pp for a 0.1 s saving). A tanh-GELU win would be a free, stackable cut.
description: Exploit, gated, following up E056. ReLU saved 0.25 s (4.8%), so GELU's fused kernels are partly compute-bound (fp32 erf), not purely bytes-bound. ReLU lost 0.54 pp because it is not smooth. Step 1, offline with no repo change: on the E049 code with synthetic channels_last batch-2000 data, compile the 20/24/28 px whitening-detached steps and the 32 px full, group-1-frozen and group-1+2-frozen steps under three activations in all conv groups: exact GELU (baseline), GELU(approximate='tanh') and SiLU. Measure GPU kernel time per step (20 steps each, torch.profiler) and weight it by the tip's per-phase step counts. Step 2 runs only if a candidate projects a saving of ≥1.5% (≥0.08 s). In that case, commit the cheapest candidate that qualifies, preferring tanh-GELU on equal savings because it matches exact GELU to about 1e-3. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E049's 60 draws, then the frozen gate. If no candidate reaches 1.5%, close H6.5's activation branch with no run.

expected: Time −1 to −2.5% (about −0.05 to −0.13 s: about 32 fewer steps of fixed cost, plus better tile use on 9×9/11×11 maps). 40-draw mean −0.25 to +0.05 pp (median −0.08). A loss of ≤ saving / 0.77 s/pp (about ≤0.12 pp) supports H5.1.3: under Muon, early steps are cheap to merge, and the cut stacks with the top-up ideas. A loss of ≥0.15 pp supports H5.2.1 (early accuracy is per-step, consistent with E045) and closes the batch axis toward larger batches.
description: Explore, the decisive pair H5.1.3 vs H5.2.1 (larger early batch). Effects near 0.1 pp are now resolvable because σ_build ≈ 0 lets 2 builds × 20 seeds stand in for 40 seeds. On the E049 tip, use batch 3000 instead of 2000 during the 20 px and 24 px phases only (the first 40% of data passes, so about 95 → about 63 steps). Key the LR triangle, whitening detach and resolution switches to data progress (samples seen), as E045 did, so they land at the same data point. Scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×1.5) in that phase and leave the Muon per-step lr unchanged. Lookahead stays every 5 steps (alpha is near 0 this early). The 28/32 px phases, both freezes and the Lookahead tail are identical to E049. Capture batch-3000 graphs at 20/24 px (full and whitening-detached variants) in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on, and check peak memory. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E049's 60 draws.
note: ideate: Superseded and low value. E061 showed that removing 12 early 20 px steps outright costs only −0.02 pp on fresh seeds, and the early-trim dose idea tests the 'early steps are nearly free' question more directly. Merging early batches at fixed data passes saves only per-step overhead (~5% of step time, E011/E047), about 0.05 s, which is below break-even for any measurable loss. The committee forecast 0/4 improve votes. The idea also still targets the E049 tip rather than E061.

expected: Time about −0.15 s (12 × ~13 ms), to about 4.86–4.90 s (−3%). 40-draw mean −0.20 to +0.02 pp vs E061 (median −0.07). A loss of ≤0.15 pp beats the 0.77 s/pp dial and makes this the tip if the gate passes. Caveat: the population may land near 0.7525, where a single committed build passes the local 0.753 bar only ~40% of the time. A loss of ≥0.2 pp means the warm-up now gets too compressed and the early-trim dial stops at 225.
description: Exploit: the second step of the early-trim dose curve. E061 removed 12 steps from the 20 px phase for −3.0% time at −0.02 pp on 40 fresh draws. On the E061 tip (225 steps; 20/24/28/32 px at about 59/24/71/71 steps), remove 12 more steps from the 20 px phase only (225 → 213; 20 px about 47 steps). The 24, 28 and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening detach, the group-1 freeze (last absolute steps) and the group-2 freeze (last absolute steps) keep the same absolute positions. The LR triangle and Lookahead ramp stretch to the new total as fractions, as in E041/E061. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (40 draws) against E061's 40 draws, then apply the frozen gate (μ̂ − 1.64·σ_tot ≥ 0.75 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 on the single committed build, no rebuilds). Record per-step CUDA-event time. This settles W6's crux: do early 20 px steps stay nearly free beyond 225?
note: E063 crashed: fix and relaunch, or drop it

expected: About −1.1 ms per 32 px full step (conv MACs: g3.conv1 ×0.875, conv2/3 ×0.77) and a larger relative cut in the frozen steps. Time −2.5 to −4% (about −0.12 to −0.20 s), to about 4.82–4.90 s. 40-draw mean −0.30 to 0 pp (median −0.13). A rate of ≥1.0 s/pp supports re-opening H2.5 at the new dial. A rate of ≤0.7 s/pp, or a loss of ≥0.3 pp, means 100-way late capacity is binding and width cuts stay closed.
description: Exploit, re-pricing the width axis at the new dial. Width cuts were rejected at the old ~1.5 s/pp dial: E010 576→512 gave ~1.4 s/pp, and E021 group 2 gave ~1.0 s/pp on possibly selection-biased seeds. Both beat the re-measured post-freeze dial of 0.77 s/pp (E059). Group 3 is the only group that trains on every step, frozen phases included, so its share of time has grown since E010. On the E061 tip, narrow only group 3 from 512 to 448 channels (a multiple of 64, so tiles stay aligned). Group 3's conv1 becomes 384→448, conv2/3 448→448, and the head takes 448 inputs. Muon lr/wd, schedules, freezes, detach, resolution and Lookahead stay unchanged. The init RNG draw order changes, which is a seed re-draw; the 40 draws absorb it. Recapture every resolution and step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Record per-step CUDA-event time per phase. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. Decision variable: the rate Δtime/Δacc against 0.77 s/pp. Above ~1.0 s/pp, follow up with narrowing plus a +0.25-epoch top-up; that pairing has a positive net value.
note: ideate: All 4 members forecast no improvement (0/4 improve votes): the group-3 width cut is expected at about the dial's rate or worse (E010 precedent ~1.4 s/pp on 100 classes, with late capacity still binding). A cut at the dial rate cannot buy the ~0.13 pp of local margin the binding H4 constraint needs, so it is dominated by the time-neutral boosters now queued.

expected: Time −3.5 to −5% (about −0.18 to −0.25 s), to about 4.77–4.85 s. 40-draw mean −0.45 to −0.05 pp (median −0.2). It beats the dial if the loss is ≤ saving/0.77 (≈0.25–0.3 pp). Then pair it with a +0.25-epoch top-up for a net cut of ~0.1 s at equal accuracy. A loss of ≥0.4 pp means early depth carries the 100-way features and closes H2.5's depth branch.
description: Explore, re-priced: an open Lvl3 that was dropped as I034 when the break-even rate was ~1.5 s/pp. At 0.77 s/pp the break-even loss for a ~0.2 s cut is ~0.26 pp. airbench94 uses 2 convs per group, while this airbench96-style port uses 3. On the E061 tip, remove only the third conv of group 1 (128→128 at 15×15, with its BN-GELU), keeping the residual add and the pool structure otherwise intact. Group-1 conv2/3 cost ~1.9 ms fwd+bwd each per full 32 px step, plus memory-bound BN/GELU on 128×15×15, and they run unfrozen for 75% of steps. The group-1 freeze, whitening detach, group-2 freeze, schedules and Lookahead stay unchanged. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. Record per-step time per phase.
note: H2.5.2 retired

expected: Time −0.09 to −0.12 s (about −2%; E040 measured −2.2%), to about 4.90–4.93 s. 40-draw mean −0.20 to 0 pp (median −0.08). A loss of ≤0.12 pp beats the dial and supports H2.3.8. A loss of ≥0.18 pp confirms that the 20→28 px jump is too large on fresh seeds and closes the early-resolution dial at 20/24/28/32.
description: Re-test, on unbiased seeds, a near-miss rejected on selection-biased ones. E040 (24 px bridge → 20 px) read −0.28 pp on seeds 3–12 right after those seeds selected E036. E041 read −0.20 on the same biased set, yet its successor E061 measured −0.02 pp on fresh seeds. The H4.4 bias (~0.2 pp) therefore explains most of E040's deficit. On the E061 tip, run the 24 px phase's ~24 steps at 20 px instead (20/28/32 px; the 28 and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts and positions). The LR triangle, Lookahead, detach and freeze schedules are unchanged. The 20 px variants are already captured; the 24 px graphs can be dropped from build. error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Run it after the early-trim dose idea so the two early-phase cuts are judged single-factor. If both pass, stack them in a later idea.
note: H2.3.8 retired

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 40-draw mean −0.25 to +0.20 pp (median −0.03). A gain of ≥0.12 pp supports H1.5.5 and funds one more 12-step early trim. A loss of ≥0.12 pp shows LS 0.3 regularizes the Lookahead average, which closes LS tuning and with it the last cheap scalar booster.
description: Explore, a time-neutral booster on an axis never tested on unbiased seeds. LS was 'flat' between 0.2 and 0.3 only at 3-seed power (E013). E032's −0.23 pp for LS → 0 late came on seeds 3–12 right after they selected E027, the same H4.4 pattern that inflated E040 and E041. Hiverge uses LS ~0.09. On the E061 tip, change only label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.15 in every phase (a midpoint toward Hiverge, less risky than 0.1 for a 100-way head). Pass LS as a constant in the compiled loss and recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws. A gain is worth ~0.12 s per 0.15 pp at the dial and can be cashed in by the early-trim ideas.
note: ideate: The committee forecasts it flat (1/4 improve, conflict 0), and whether reduced LS can help depends on whether the recipe under-fits. The new H8.2.1 diagnostic decides that at almost no cost. LS 0.15 is re-queued only if the diagnostic shows fitting saturation (train top-1 ≥97%).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.02 s). If decay compression drives E055's cost, the 60-draw mean rises +0.05 to +0.15 pp (median +0.07). That is a free booster and would raise the local pass probability from ~50% to ~65%. A change within ±0.03 pp means the cost of earlier freezes comes from lost late steps; the freeze point itself (H2.6.12) is then the lever. A loss ≥0.1 pp means group 1 needs to reach LR 0 before the detach.
description: Exploit: a time-neutral test that separates the two parts of the freeze-dose cost. On the E061 tip (225 steps), change only the end point of the group-1 LR anneal (conv filters on Muon; BN params on SGD): it moves from 75% to 80% of steps, so group 1's LR decays more slowly over the whole run. The group-1 detach stays at 75% (same absolute step), so the frozen variant covers exactly the same steps and time is unchanged. At the detach, the group-1 LR is then about 5/57 ≈ 9% of peak instead of 0. E009 and C0021 say the LR floor does not matter under Lookahead averaging. Whitening detach, group-2 freeze, resolution, step count, Lookahead and LS are unchanged. If the LR is a GPU tensor table, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (60 draws) against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. This is the time-neutral form of H2.6.13. E055's −0.29 pp moved the anneal end and the detach together; this moves only the anneal.

expected: Time +0.07 to +0.10 s (~+1.8%, to ~5.10 s). 60-draw mean +0.05 to +0.25 pp (median +0.12). Break-even at 0.77 s/pp is ~0.12 pp. A gain ≥0.15 pp beats the dial and should be spent on the early trim (I099), for a net time cut at higher margin. A gain ≤0.05 pp confirms that 75% sits on the flat side of the knee, so the freeze point is settled.
description: Exploit, a margin buyer priced against the dial. On the E061 tip, move the group-1 detach and its LR anneal end together from 75% to 80% of steps (~11 more unfrozen 32 px steps at ~7.7 ms each, ≈ +0.09 s). Step count (225), whitening detach (6%), group-2 freeze (75→90% anneal, detach at 90%), resolution, LR triangle, Lookahead and LS are unchanged. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Record per-step CUDA-event time. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Rationale: E055 shows a steep dose (−0.29 pp for freezing 4% earlier). E028's 'free' reading at 75% was a 10-seed result with SE ~0.12 pp, so the slope may continue past 75%. Run after the anneal-only idea, if possible, so its result can be split into anneal and step components.
note: committee veto AUDIT: run it to measure the veto

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 60-draw mean −0.10 to +0.20 pp (median +0.06). A gain ≥0.12 pp supports H1.5.6 and H8.1, and funds ~0.1 s of trimming. The next point is then ×2 or a momentum retune. A loss ≥0.1 pp puts the optimum at ≤0.24 and closes the upward lr direction.
description: Exploit, a time-neutral optimizer booster on the axis H8 says is load-bearing. On the E061 tip, raise the Muon lr for every conv-filter group from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5). The per-group schedules (group-1 anneal to 75%, group-2 anneal 75→90%), momentum 0.6, wd ×0.5, the SGD groups, batch, step count, resolution, freezes, Lookahead and LS are all unchanged. If the lr is baked into the graph, recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws (SE of the difference ~0.06 pp), then the frozen gate. E014 read +0.09 pp at 3 seeds on the higher-wd base. E062 shows that per-step update quality dominates at ~225 steps, and the CIFAR-10 airbench94 lr was never retuned for this regime.

expected: Step 1: optimizer overhead beyond NS is ~0.2–0.5 ms/step (median), i.e. 0.05–0.1 s/trial. If it qualifies: time −1 to −2% (to ~4.93–4.97 s); accuracy within rebuild noise (±0.05 pp on 40 draws). If Step 1 shows the 0.28 s E062 gap is fully explained by NS + SGD-vs-Muon GPU time, close H2.2.5 (refuted) with no run.
description: Exploit, a systems change with identical math, gated on a measurement (crux of W3/W5). Step 1, offline on E061 code with synthetic batch-2000 data: put CUDA events around the optimizer section of each step variant (Muon momentum + NS + update for the 3 filter groups, SGD groups, Lookahead). Record the GPU time and the host wall gap per step, and count the kernels and DtoD memcpys per step (E076 found ~51/step from mutated-input write-backs). Step 2 runs only if the non-NS optimizer overhead × 225 steps projects ≥0.05 s. Then replace the per-group Muon calls with one compiled function that does a foreach Nesterov momentum update over all filter tensors and NS with batched bmm over shape-identical filters (g1.conv2/3, g2.conv2/3, g3.conv2/3 each stack to one bmm; singletons run alone). Per-group LRs are read from one GPU-resident [groups × steps] table indexed by a GPU step counter, so there are no Python scalars and no write-back copies. Frozen groups are excluded through static per-variant parameter lists. Check offline that the updates match the current code to bf16 tolerance over 20 steps. Recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge time on per-step CUDA events plus 2 builds' wall time, and accuracy on 2 builds × seeds 33–52 (must sit within 0.08 pp of E061), then the frozen gate.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 60-draw mean −0.30 to +0.15 pp (median −0.05). A gain ≥0.12 pp supports H8.1.1: then test 0.7 combined with any lr gain. A loss ≥0.12 pp refutes it and points the next probe at 0.5 (the critical-batch direction).
description: Explore, a decisive test of the Muon-momentum crux. On the E061 tip, change only the Muon momentum for every conv-filter group from 0.6 to 0.8 (Nesterov kept; lr, wd, per-group schedules, batch, step count, freezes, Lookahead and LS unchanged). If the momentum is a baked constant, recapture every variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on 3 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 against E061's 40 draws, then the frozen gate. Two accounts disagree. Muon critical-batch theory (b* falls at higher β, with batch 2000 already large) and the CIFAR-100 critical-damping result predict harm. H8.1 predicts that more momentum smooths per-step noise in a 225-step run with heavy LS and Lookahead resets, and gains. The 0.6 value comes from CIFAR-10 airbench94 and has never been varied here.

expected: Task metrics unchanged (E061: ~5.02 s, ~0.753). Predicted clean train top-1 is 85–93% (median ~89%), i.e. under-fitting, and the averaged weights read 1–3 pp above the fast weights. If ≤90%: regularizer additions (LS ↓, jitter, ghost BN) stay deprioritized and optimizer/freeze-later boosters lead. If ≥97%: the recipe is fitting-saturated, so queue LS 0.15 (H1.5.5) and jitter (H1.5.8) on 60 draws and deprioritize Muon retuning.
description: Explore diagnostic, offline, outside submissions/arena/, with no recipe change. It routes the remaining booster search. Run an instrumented copy of the E061 tip on real training data for seeds 33–35. After train() returns, evaluate the final averaged weights (eval mode, as in the submission) on a fixed 10k subset of the 50k training images at 32 px with no augmentation. Record top-1 and plain CE (no LS). For contrast, also record the same metrics for the fast weights just before the final Lookahead copy, and train top-1 on the last 32 px epoch's augmented batches (logged during training). Never touch the test set beyond the harness's normal eval. Write the numbers to the notebook.
